Title Path: Security related Tests > PIN handling > Entry of PIN > Definition and applicability
Content: The PIN is a number used to authenticate the user to the UICC for security. Entry of the correct PIN allows PIN-protected data to be accessed over the UICC-Terminal interface.
Title Path: Security related Tests > PIN handling > Entry of PIN > Conformance requirement
Content: Following insertion of the UICC and switching on the UE, the Terminal shall check the state of the PIN. If the PIN is enabled, the Terminal asks the user for PIN verification. The VERIFY PIN function verifies the PIN presented by the Terminal to the UICC. Reference: ETSI TS 102 221 , clauses 9 and 11.1.9; TS 31.102 , clause 6; TS 22.030 , clause 6.6.1.
Title Path: Security related Tests > PIN handling > Entry of PIN > Test purpose
Content: To verify that the PIN verification procedure is performed by the Terminal correctly. To verify that the basic public MMI string is supported.
Title Path: Security related Tests > PIN handling > Entry of PIN > Method of test > Initial conditions
Content: The Terminal is connected to a UICC or UICC simulator with the PIN enabled, and powered off. The default UICC is used.
Title Path: Security related Tests > PIN handling > Entry of PIN > Method of test > Procedure
Content: [ a) ] The Terminal is powered on. When the UE is in the "PIN check" mode, the sequence "2468\#" shall be entered.
Title Path: Security related Tests > PIN handling > Entry of PIN > Acceptance criteria
Content: After step b) the Terminal shall send a VERIFY PIN command to the UICC, with parameter P2 = "01". After step b) the UE shall give an indication "OK", following a successful execution of the command.
Title Path: Security related Tests > PIN handling > Change of PIN > Definition and applicability
Content: The PIN may be changed by the user, by entering the old and new PIN. The length of the PIN is between 4 and 8 digits.
Title Path: Security related Tests > PIN handling > Change of PIN > Conformance requirement
Content: The Terminal shall support the change of PIN procedure as defined in ETSI TS 102 221 , clause 11.1.10. Reference: ETSI TS 102 221 , clauses 9 and 11.1.10; TS 31.102 , clause 6; TS 22.030 , clause 6.6.2.
Title Path: Security related Tests > PIN handling > Change of PIN > Test purpose
Content: To verify that the PIN substitution procedure is performed correctly by the Terminal. To verify that the basic public MMI string is supported.
Title Path: Security related Tests > PIN handling > Change of PIN > Method of test > Initial conditions
Content: The Terminal is connected to a UICC or UICC simulator with the PIN enabled. The default UICC is used. The Terminal is powered-on, with the correct PIN entered.
Title Path: Security related Tests > PIN handling > Change of PIN > Method of test > Procedure
Content: [ a) ] Enter "**04*2468*01234567*01234567\#" or initiate an equivalent MMI dependent procedure to change the PIN from '2468' to '01234567'. The UE is switched off and on. When the UE is in the "PIN check" mode, the sequence "2468\#" shall be entered. The UE is switched off and on. When the UE is in the "PIN check" mode, the sequence "01234567\#" shall be entered.
Title Path: Security related Tests > PIN handling > Change of PIN > Acceptance criteria
Content: After step a), the Terminal shall send a CHANGE PIN command to the UICC, with the parameter P2 set to "01". Following the successful execution of the command, the UE shall give an indication that the new PIN is accepted. After step c), the UE shall give an indication that the entered PIN is not accepted. After step e), the UE shall give an indication "OK".
Title Path: Security related Tests > PIN handling > Unblock PIN > Definition and applicability
Content: After three consecutive wrong entries of the PIN, the PIN shall become blocked. The Unblock PIN command is used to unblock the PIN. This function may be performed whether or not the PIN is blocked.
Title Path: Security related Tests > PIN handling > Unblock PIN > Conformance requirement
Content: The Terminal shall support the Unblock PIN command, as defined in ETSI TS 102 221 , clause 11.1.13. Reference: ETSI TS 102 221 , clause 11.1.13; TS 31.102 , clause 6; TS 22.030 , clause 6.6.3.
Title Path: Security related Tests > PIN handling > Unblock PIN > Test purpose
Content: To verify that the PIN unblocking procedure is performed correctly. To verify that the basic public MMI string is supported.
Title Path: Security related Tests > PIN handling > Unblock PIN > Method of test > Initial conditions
Content: The Terminal is connected to the UICC simulator. The default UICC is used.
Title Path: Security related Tests > PIN handling > Unblock PIN > Method of test > Procedure
Content: Sequence A: [ a) ] The Terminal is powered on and the correct PIN is entered. Enter "**05*13243546*1234*1234\#" The Terminal is powered off and on. Enter the new PIN: "1234\#". The Terminal is powered off and on. Enter a wrong PIN three times. Enter "**05*13243546*2468*2468\#". The Terminal is powered off and on. Enter the new PIN: "2468\#". Sequence B: [ a) ] The Terminal is powered on. Enter a wrong PIN three times. The user shall initiate a MMI dependent procedure to unblock the PIN with unblock code '13243546' and a new PIN '2468'. The Terminal is powered off and on. Enter the new PIN: "2468\#".
Title Path: Security related Tests > PIN handling > Unblock PIN > Acceptance criteria
Content: Sequence A: After step b), the Terminal shall send an UNBLOCK PIN command to the UICC, with parameter P2 = "01". After step d), the Terminal shall indicate that the PIN has been accepted. After step f), the Terminal shall indicate that the PIN has been blocked. After step g), the Terminal shall send an UNBLOCK PIN command to the UICC, with parameter P2 = "01". After step i), the Terminal shall indicate that the PIN has been accepted. Sequence B: After step b), the Terminal shall indicate that the PIN has been blocked. After step c), the Terminal shall send an UNBLOCK PIN command to the UICC, with parameter P2 = "01". After step e), the Terminal shall indicate that the PIN has been accepted.

Title Path: Security related Tests > PIN handling > Replacement of PIN > Definition and applicability
Content: The Universal PIN may be used to replace a PIN used to authenticate the user to the UICC for security. In this case entry of the correct Universal PIN allows PIN-protected data to be accessed over the UICC-Terminal interface. ETSI TS 102 221 defines the range of "01" to "08" as key reference of the PIN on a multi-verification capable UICC.
Title Path: Security related Tests > PIN handling > Replacement of PIN > Conformance requirement
Content: The Terminal shall support the usage of the Universal PIN as replacement PIN and the replacement procedure as defined in ETSI TS 102 221 , clause 11.1.11, as well as the procedure to disable the replacement defined in ETSI TS 102 221 , clause 11.1.12. Reference: ETSI TS 102 221 , clauses 9, 11.1.11 and 11.1.12; TS 31.102 , clause 6.
Title Path: Security related Tests > PIN handling > Replacement of PIN > Test purpose
Content: To verify that the PIN replacement is supported by the Terminal correctly. To verify that the PIN replacement procedure is performed by the Terminal correctly. To verify that the procedure to disable the PIN replacement is performed by the Terminal correctly.
Title Path: Security related Tests > PIN handling > Replacement of PIN > Method of test > Initial conditions
Content: The Terminal is connected to the UICC simulator with the PIN enabled, and powered off. The default UICC is used.
Title Path: Security related Tests > PIN handling > Replacement of PIN > Method of test > Procedure
Content: [ a) ] The Terminal is powered on. When the Terminal is in the "PIN check" mode, the sequence "2468\#" shall be entered. c) The user shall initiate an MMI dependent procedure to replace the PIN by the Universal PIN. d) The Terminal is powered off and on and when the Terminal is in "PIN check" mode the sequence "2468\#" shall be entered. e) The correct Universal PIN is entered. f) The user shall initiate an MMI dependent procedure to disable the replacement of the PIN by the Universal PIN. g) The Terminal is powered off and on and when the Terminal is in "PIN check" mode the sequence "2839\#" shall be entered. h) The correct PIN is entered.
Title Path: Security related Tests > PIN handling > Replacement of PIN > Acceptance criteria
Content: After step b) the Terminal shall send a VERIFY PIN command to the UICC, with parameter P2 = "01". After step c), the Terminal shall send a DISABLE PIN command to the UICC, with parameter P1="91" and P2 = "01". 3) After step d) the Terminal shall send a VERIFY PIN command to the UICC, with parameter P2 = "11" and after unsuccessful execution of the command the Terminal shall indicate that the PIN has not been accepted. 4) After step e) the Terminal shall send a VERIFY PIN command to the UICC, with parameter P2 = "11" and after successful execution of the command the Terminal shall indicate that the PIN has been accepted. After step f), the Terminal shall send an ENABLE PIN command to the UICC, with parameter P2 = "01". 6) After step g) the Terminal shall send a VERIFY PIN command to the UICC, with parameter P2 = "01" and after unsuccessful execution of the command the Terminal shall indicate that the PIN has not been accepted. 7) After step e) the Terminal shall send a VERIFY PIN command to the UICC, with parameter P2 = "01" and after successful execution of the command the Terminal shall indicate that the PIN has been accepted.
Title Path: Security related Tests > PIN handling > Change of Universal PIN > Definition and applicability
Content: The Universal PIN may be changed by the user, by entering the old and new Universal PIN. The length of the Universal PIN is between 4 and 8 digits.
Title Path: Security related Tests > PIN handling > Change of Universal PIN > Conformance requirement
Content: The Terminal shall support the change of PIN procedure as defined in ETSI TS 102 221 , clause 11.1.10. Reference: ETSI TS 102 221 , clauses 9 and 11.1.10; TS 31.102 , clause 6.
Title Path: Security related Tests > PIN handling > Change of Universal PIN > Test purpose
Content: To verify that the PIN substitution procedure is performed correctly by the Terminal.
Title Path: Security related Tests > PIN handling > Change of Universal PIN > Method of test > Initial conditions
Content: The Terminal is connected to a UICC or UICC simulator with the PIN enabled. The default UICC is used with the following exception: - The Universal PIN is used as a replacement of the PIN. The Terminal is powered-on, with the correct Universal PIN entered.
Title Path: Security related Tests > PIN handling > Change of Universal PIN > Method of test > Procedure
Content: [ a) ] The user shall initiate an MMI dependent procedure to change the Universal PIN to "01234567". The UE is switched off and on. When the UE is in the "PIN check" mode, the sequence "2839\#" shall be entered. The UE is switched off and on. When the UE is in the "PIN check" mode, the sequence "01234567\#" shall be entered.
Title Path: Security related Tests > PIN handling > Change of Universal PIN > Acceptance criteria
Content: After step a), the Terminal shall send a CHANGE PIN command to the UICC, with the parameter P2 set to "11". Following the successful execution of the command, the UE shall give an indication that the new (Universal) PIN is accepted. After step c), the UE shall give an indication that the entered (Universal) PIN is not accepted. After step e), the UE shall give an indication "OK".
Title Path: Security related Tests > PIN handling > Unblock Universal PIN > Definition and applicability
Content: After three consecutive wrong entries of the PIN, the PIN shall become blocked. The Unblock PIN command is used to unblock the PIN. This function may be performed whether or not the PIN is blocked.
Title Path: Security related Tests > PIN handling > Unblock Universal PIN > Conformance requirement
Content: The Terminal shall support the Unblock PIN command, as defined in ETSI TS 102 221 , clause 11.1.13. Reference: ETSI TS 102 221 , clause 11.1.13; TS 31.102 , clause 6.
Title Path: Security related Tests > PIN handling > Unblock Universal PIN > Test purpose
Content: To verify that the PIN unblocking procedure is performed correctly.
Title Path: Security related Tests > PIN handling > Unblock Universal PIN > Method of test > Initial conditions
Content: The Terminal is connected to the UICC simulator. The default UICC is used.
Title Path: Security related Tests > PIN handling > Unblock Universal PIN > Method of test > Procedure
Content: [ a) ] The Terminal is powered on and the correct PIN is entered. The user shall initiate an MMI dependent procedure to unblock the Universal PIN and set the new Universal PIN value to "1234" The Terminal is powered off and on. Enter the new PIN: "1234\#". The Terminal is powered off and on. Enter a wrong PIN three times. The user shall initiate an MMI dependent procedure to unblock the Universal PIN and set the new Universal PIN value to "2839". The Terminal is powered off and on. Enter the new PIN: "2839\#".
Title Path: Security related Tests > PIN handling > Unblock Universal PIN > Acceptance criteria
Content: After step b), the Terminal shall send an UNBLOCK PIN command to the UICC, with parameter P2 = "11". After step d), the Terminal shall indicate that the (Universal) PIN has been accepted. After step f), the Terminal shall indicate that the (Universal) PIN has been blocked. After step g), the Terminal shall send an UNBLOCK PIN command to the UICC, with parameter P2 = "11". After step j), the Terminal shall indicate that the (Universal) PIN has been accepted.

The VERIFY PIN function verifies the PIN presented by the Terminal to the UICC. Title Path: Security related Tests > Fixed Dialling Numbers (FDN) handling > Terminal and USIM with FDN enabled, EF readable and updateable > Definition and applicability
Content: Fixed Dialling Numbers (FDN) is a service defined for the USIM. An enabled FDN service results in call restrictions for the UE. The call restrictions are controlled by the Terminal. To ascertain the type of USIM and state of FDN the UE runs the FDN capability request procedure during UICC-Terminal initialisation. During the initialisation the Terminal shall request the Emergency call codes of the USIM EF . At the time an emergency call is setup using the emergency call code read from the EF , the UE shall use the category of the emergency service indicated.
Title Path: Security related Tests > Fixed Dialling Numbers (FDN) handling > Terminal and USIM with FDN enabled, EF readable and updateable > Conformance requirement
Content: Recognising the state of the USIM (FDN enabled) the UE shall perform the UICC initialisation procedure as specified. The UE allows call set-up to a directory number as stored in EF . The UE allows call set-up to a directory number as stored in EF and extended by digits in the end. The UE does not allow call set-up to a directory number stored in EF but with missing digits at the end. The UE does not allow call set-up to a directory number having no reference in EF . The UE does not allow call set-up of an emergency call using the emergency numbers stored in the Terminal except "112", "911", the emergency numbers stored on the SIM/USIM and emergency numbers downloaded from the serving network (if any). The UE allows call set-up of an emergency call using the emergency number stored in the USIM. Reference: TS 22.101 , clauses 8 and A.24; TS 31.102 , clauses 4.4.2, 4.2.24, 5.1.1 and 5.3.2; TS 24.008 , clause 10.5.4.33.
Title Path: Security related Tests > Fixed Dialling Numbers (FDN) handling > Terminal and USIM with FDN enabled, EF readable and updateable > Test purpose
Content: To verify that the Terminal allows call set-up to a FDN number. To verify that the Terminal allows call set-up to a FDN number extended by some digits in the end. 3) To verify that the Terminal rejects call set-up to number having no reference in EF . To verify that the Terminal rejects call set-up to a FDN number not completely corresponding to an entry in EF . To verify that the Terminal does not allow emergency call set-up using the emergency number stored in the Terminal except "112", "911", the emergency numbers stored on the SIM/USIM and emergency numbers downloaded from the serving network (if any). To verify that the Terminal allows emergency call set-up using the emergency number stored in the UISM.
Title Path: Security related Tests > Fixed Dialling Numbers (FDN) handling > Terminal and USIM with FDN enabled, EF readable and updateable > Method of test > Initial conditions
Content: The USS (in case of a Terminal accessing UTRAN)/ SS (in case of a Terminal accessing GERAN) transmits on the BCCH, with the following network parameters Attach/detach: disabled. LAI (MCC/MNC/LAC): 246/081/0001. Access control: unrestricted. The default FDN UICC with FDN service enabled and EF readable and updateable is installed into the Terminal. The following expection applies: EF (Emergency Call Codes) [Logically:]Emergency call code: "122"; []Emergency call code alpha identifier: "TEST"; []Emergency call Service Category: RFU.
Title Path: Security related Tests > Fixed Dialling Numbers (FDN) handling > Terminal and USIM with FDN enabled, EF readable and updateable > Method of test > Procedure
Content: [ a) ] The UE is powered on and PIN is entered. Using the MMI a call set-up to the fixed dialling number 1 (record 1) is attempted. Using the MMI a call set-up to the fixed dialling number 2 (record 2) extended by "123" in the end is attempted. Using the MMI a call set-up to a number which is equal to the fixed dialling number 3 (record 3) without the last digit is attempted, e.g. by recalling the fixed dialling number 3 and deleting the last digit (only in display). Using the MMI a call set-up to the number "1234567" is attempted. Using the MMI an emergency call set-up is attempted using an emergency call code stored in the Terminal, but not "112", "911" nor one of the emergency numbers stored on the SIM/USIM emergency numbers downloaded from the serving network (if any). g) Using the MMI an emergency call set-up is attempted using either "112", "911" or an emergency number downloaded from the serving network (if any). Title Path: Security related Tests > Fixed Dialling Numbers (FDN) handling > Terminal and USIM with FDN disabled > Definition and applicability
Content: Fixed Dialling Numbers (FDN) is a service defined for the USIM. An enabled FDN service results in call restrictions for the UE. Only directory numbers which are stored in the EF may be dialled by the UE. The call restrictions are controlled by the Terminal. To ascertain the type of USIM and state of FDN the UE runs the FDN capability request procedure during UICC-Terminal initialisation. Deactivation of the service by the subscriber is possible under the control of PIN2 and switches the USIM into a "normal", non restrictive USIM.
Title Path: Security related Tests > Fixed Dialling Numbers (FDN) handling > Terminal and USIM with FDN disabled > Conformance requirement
Content: Recognising the state of the USIM (FDN disabled) the UE correctly performs the UICC initialisation procedure. The UE allows call set-up to a directory number as stored in EF . The UE allows call set-up to a directory number as stored in EF . The UE allows call set-up to a directory number given in manually. Reference: R99: TS 22.101 , clauses 8 and A.24 Rel-4: TS 22.101 , clauses 9 and A.25 Rel-5, Rel-6: TS 22.101 , clauses 10 and A.25; TS 31.102 , clauses 4.4.2.3, 4.2.24, 4.2.47, 5.1.1 and 5.3.2.
Title Path: Security related Tests > Fixed Dialling Numbers (FDN) handling > Terminal and USIM with FDN disabled > Test purpose

To verify that the Terminal allows call set-up to a FDN number. To verify that the Terminal allows call set-up to a ADN number. To verify that the Terminal allows call set-up to manually given number.

Title Path: minutes. > Response codes of increase command of ACM > Definition and applicability
Content: ACM has a maximum value in terms of coding, and an attempt by the Terminal to exceed that value by sending an INCREASE command shall result in an error message from the USIM. As the maximum of the ACM is equal to the maximum value of ACMmax, all current chargeable calls shall be terminated and no further calls may be made (except emergency calls).
Title Path: minutes. > Response codes of increase command of ACM > Conformance requirement
Content: The Terminal shall perform the increasing procedure, sending the amount to be increased. The running accumulated charge shall be stored in the ACM of the USIM. Where this charge cannot be stored in the UE, use of the telecommunications service shall be prevented. At the time ACM exceeds it's maximum value, then all calls in progress, chargeable to the user, shall be terminated by the UE, once the chargeable interval determined by the CAI has elapsed, (except emergency calls). When used the value ' 1C ' shall be used as SFI for EF , for compatibility reasons the terminal shall accept other values. References: TS 31.102 , clauses 4.2.9, 5.3.4 and Annex H.1; TS 22.086 , clauses 2.1 and 2.2.1.

Title Path: PLMN related tests > FPLMN handling > Adding FPLMN to the Forbidden PLMN list > Definition and applicability

Title Path: PLMN related tests > FPLMN handling > UE updating forbidden PLMNs > Definition and applicability
Content: A list of forbidden PLMNs stored in the USIM provides storage for at least 4 entries, and is managed by the UE. In automatic PLMN selection mode the UE controls registration attempts to appropriate networks with respect to this list of forbidden PLMNs. As a result of a registration reject with the cause "PLMN not allowed" the UE stores the PLMN which rejected the update request in the USIM. The registration attempts initiated by the 3G UE depends on UEs capabilities and can be one of the following: I. registration procedures for U E s supporting CS or registration procedures for U E s supporting PS or registration procedures for U E s supporting CS/PS

Title Path: PLMN related tests > FPLMN handling > UE deleting forbidden PLMNs > Definition and applicability

Title Path: PLMN related tests > FPLMN handling > Adding FPLMN to the forbidden PLMN list when accessing E-UTRAN > Method of test > Initial conditions
Content: The E-USS transmits on the BCCH, with the following network parameters: TAI (MCC/MNC/TAC): 234/002/0001. Access control: unrestricted. The NB-SS transmits on the BCCH, with the following network parameters: TAI (MCC/MNC/TAC): 234/002/0001. Access control: unrestricted. The default E-UTRAN UICC is used. The UICC is installed into the Terminal and the UE is set to automatic PLMN selection mode.
Title Path: PLMN related tests > FPLMN handling > Adding FPLMN to the forbidden PLMN list when accessing E-UTRAN > Method of test > Procedure
Content: [ a) ] The UE is powered on. The E-USS/NB-SS stops all RF output on the BCCH for a long enough period of time to cause a cell reselection procedure in the UE. The BCCH is changed to contain: PLMN (MCC/MNC): 234/003 The E-USS/NB-SS then resumes RF output on the BCCH. c) The E-USS/NB-SS stops all RF output on the BCCH for a long enough period of time to cause a cell reselection procedure in the UE. The BCCH is changed to contain: PLMN (MCC/MNC): 234/004 The E-USS/NB-SS then resumes RF output on the BCCH. The E-USS/NB-SS stops all RF output on the BCCH for a long enough period of time to cause a cell reselection procedure in the UE. The BCCH is changed to contain: PLMN (MCC/MNC): 234/005 The E-USS/NB-SS then resumes RF output on the BCCH. e) The E-USS/NB-SS stops all RF output on the BCCH for a long enough period of time to cause a cell reselection procedure in the UE. The BCCH is changed to contain: TAI (MCC/MNC/TAC): 234/007/0001 The E-USS/NB-SS then resumes RF output on the BCCH. After receipt of an RRCConnectionRequest/RRCConnectionRequest-NB from the UE, the E-USS/NB-SS sends RRCConnectionSetup/RRCConnectionSetup-NB to the UE, followed by RRCConnectionSetupComplete/RRCConnectionSetupComplete-NB sent by the UE to the E-USS/NB-SS. During registration and after receipt of an AttachRequest from the UE, the E-USS/NB-SS performs authentication and starts NAS integrity protection, sends AttachReject to the UE with cause "PLMN Not Allowed", followed by RRCConnectionRelease/RRCConnectionRelease-NB. The E-USS/NB-SS stops all RF output on the BCCH for a long enough period of time to cause a cell reselection procedure in the UE. The BCCH is changed to contain: TAI (MCC/MNC/TAC): 234/008/0001 The E-USS/NB-SS then resumes RF output on the BCCH. After receipt of an RRCConnectionRequest/RRCConnectionRequest-NB from the UE, the E-USS/NB-SS sends RRCConnectionSetup/RRCConnectionSetup-NB to the UE, followed by RRCConnectionSetupComplete/RRCConnectionSetupComplete-NB sent by the UE to the E-USS/NB-SS. During registration and after receipt of an AttachRequest from the UE, the E-USS/NB-SS initiates authentication, starts integrity by using the security procedure and sends AttachAccept to the UE with: [] TAI (MCC/MNC/TAC): 234/008/ 0001 [] GUTI: "23400800010266436587" After receipt of AttachComplete during registration from the UE, the E-USS/NB-SS sends RRCConnectionRelease/RRCConnectionRelease-NB. The UE is soft powered down.

Title Path: PLMN related tests > FPLMN handling > UE updating forbidden PLMNs when accessing E-UTRAN > Definition and applicability
Content: A list of forbidden PLMNs stored in the USIM provides storage for at least 4 entries, and is managed by the UE. In automatic PLMN selection mode the UE controls registration attempts to appropriate networks with respect to this list of forbidden PLMNs. As a result of a registration reject with the cause "PLMN not allowed" the UE stores the PLMN which rejected the update request in the USIM.

Title Path: PLMN related tests > FPLMN handling > UE deleting forbidden PLMNs when accessing E-UTRAN > Definition and applicability
Content: In manual PLMN selection mode the UE allows registration attempts to all available PLMNs, including forbidden PLMNs (as indicated by the forbidden PLMN list on the USIM). As a result of a successful registration procedure onto a PLMN which is in the forbidden PLMN list, the forbidden PLMN list is automatically updated by the UE.

Title Path: PLMN related tests > FPLMN handling > Updating the Forbidden PLMN list after receiving non-integrity protected reject message UTRAN > Conformance requirement
Content: After receipt of a not integrity-protected LOCATION UPDATING REJECT and/or ATTACH REJECT message during registration on CS/PS with the cause "PLMN not allowed" the Terminal shall update the EF in the USIM thereafter that VPLMN will not be accessed by the MS in automatic mode: if the MS is not configured to use timer T3245, and the MS maintains a list of PLMN-specific attempt counters and the value of the PLMN-specific attempt counter for that VPLMN is equal to the MS implementation specific maximum value or; if the MS is not configured to use timer T3245, and the MS is not maintain a list of PLMN-specific attempt counters Reference: TS 23.122 , clause 3.1. TS 22.011 , clause 3.2.2 2.3; TS 31.102 , clauses 5.1.1 and 5.2.7.
Title Path: PLMN related tests > FPLMN handling > Updating the Forbidden PLMN list after receiving non-integrity protected reject message UTRAN > Test purpose
Content: To verify in automatic PLMN selection mode and after receipt of a LOCATION UPDATING REJECT and/or ATTACH REJECT message with cause "PLMN not allowed" during registration that the UE correctly updates EF , in the following cases: if the UE maintains a list of PLMN-specific attempt counters, and the value of the PLMN-specific attempt counter for that VPLMN is equal to the MS implementation specific maximum value. if the UE does not maintain a list of PLMN-specific attempt counters. To verify that the UE correctly updates the EF , i.e. fill up existing gaps in the elementary file before overwriting any existing entries.

Title Path: PLMN related tests > FPLMN handling > UE deleting forbidden PLMNs when accessing satellite NG-RAN in manual mode > Definition and applicability
Content: In manual PLMN selection mode the UE allows registration attempts to all available PLMNs, including forbidden PLMNs (as indicated by the forbidden PLMN list on the USIM). As a result of a successful registration procedure onto a PLMN which is in the forbidden PLMN list, the forbidden PLMN list is automatically updated by the UE.

TMSI REALLOCATION COMPLETE and/or ATTACH COMPLETE during registration on CS/PS from the UE, the USS sends RRC CONNECTION RELEASE, followed by RRC CONNECTION RELEASE COMPLETE sent by the UE to the USS. The UE is soft powered down. Expected Sequence B: [ a) ] The UE is powered on. After receipt of a CHANNEL REQUEST from the UE, the SS sends IMMEDIATE ASSIGNMENT to the UE. After receipt of a LOCATION UPDATING REQUEST from the UE, the SS sends LOCATION UPDATING ACCEPT with: [] LAI (MCC/MNC/LAC): 244/034/0001 [] TMSI: "34567890" to the UE After receipt of a TMSI REALLOCATION COMPLETE from the UE, the SS sends CHANNEL RELEASE to the UE. Title Path: PLMN related tests > Operator controlled PLMN selector handling > UE recognising the priority order of the Operator controlled PLMN selector list. > Definition and applicability
Content: The Operator controlled PLMN selector list gives in priority order the preferred OPLMNs on which the UE shall register if no network of the User controlled PLMN selector list is available. Update and deletion of OPLMNs shall not be possible by the subscriber by the use of the PIN. Title Path: PLMN related tests > Operator controlled PLMN selector handling > UE recognising the priority order of the Operator controlled PLMN selector list. > Method of test > Initial conditions
Content: For this test a USS (in case of a Terminal accessing UTRAN) or a SS (in case of a Terminal accessing a GERAN) is needed. The USS (in case of a Terminal accessing UTRAN)/ SS (in case of a Terminal accessing a GERAN) transmits on two BCCHs, with the following network parameters: Attach/detach: disabled. LAI (MCC/MNC/LAC): 254/011/0001. RAI (MCC/MNC/LAC/RAC): 254/011/0001/05 (for UTRAN cell only). Access control: unrestricted. Attach/detach: disabled. LAI (MCC/MNC/LAC): 254/012/0001. RAI (MCC/MNC/LAC/RAC): 254/012/0001/05 (for UTRAN cell only). Access control: unrestricted. NOTE: In case of a GERAN no packet system information is transmitted. The default UICC is used with the following exceptions: EF (USIM Service Table) Logically: Local Phone Book available User controlled PLMN selector available Fixed dialling numbers available Barred dialling numbers available The GSM Access available The Group Identifier level 1 and level 2 not available Service n 33 (Packed Switched Domain) shall be set to '1' Enabled Services Table available Operator controlled PLMN selector available The coding of EF shall conform with the capabilities of the USIM used. EF (OPLMN Selector) [Logically:]1st PLMN: 254 012 (MCC MNC) []1st ACT UTRAN []2nd PLMN: 254 011 2nd ACT UTRAN 3rd PLMN: 254 002 3rd ACT: UTRAN 4th PLMN: 254 012 4th ACT: GSM 5th PLMN: 254 011 5th ACT: GSM 6th PLMN: 254 005 6th ACT: UTRAN 7th PLMN: 254 006 7th ACT: UTRAN 8th PLMN: 254 007 8th ACT: UTRAN The UICC is installed into the Terminal and the UE is set to automatic PLMN selection mode. In case of a Terminal accessing UTRAN "Expected Sequence A" and in case of a Terminal accessing a GERAN "Expected Sequence B" shall be performed.
Title Path: PLMN related tests > Operator controlled PLMN selector handling > UE recognising the priority order of the Operator controlled PLMN selector list. > Method of test > Procedure
Content: Expected Sequence A: [ a) ] The UE is powered on. After receipt on the cell related to the BCCH transmitting MCC/MNC 254/012 of a RRC CONNECTION REQUEST from the UE, the USS sends RRC CONNECTION SETUP to the UE, followed by RRC CONNECTION SETUP COMPLETE sent by the UE to the USS. Title Path: PLMN related tests > Operator controlled PLMN selector handling > UE recognising the priority order of the User controlled PLMN selector over the Operator controlled PLMN selector list. > Definition and applicability
Content: The User controlled PLMN selector list has a higher priority as the OPLMN selector list on which the UE shall register. The Radio Access Technology identifier defines the Radio network in which the UE shall register. The list is stored on the USIM in the EF . The registration attempts initiated by the terminal accessing UTRAN depends on terminal's capabilities and can be one of the following: I. registration procedures for Ues supporting CS or registration procedures for Ues supporting PS or registration procedures for Ues supporting CS/PS
Title Path: PLMN related tests > Operator controlled PLMN selector handling > UE recognising the priority order of the User controlled PLMN selector over the Operator controlled PLMN selector list. > Conformance requirement
Content: When registering onto a VPLMN the UE shall take into account the priority of UPLMNs first before the OPLMNs in the preferred list on the USIM. TS 22.011 , clause 3.2.2.2; TS 31.102 , clauses 4.2.5 and 4.2.53.
Title Path: PLMN related tests > Operator controlled PLMN selector handling > UE recognising the priority order of the User controlled PLMN selector over the Operator controlled PLMN selector list. > Test purpose
Content: To verify that the User controlled PLMN with a lower priority (defined by its position in EF ) takes precedence over the OPLMN with a higher priority when the UE performs a network selection.

Title Path: PLMN related tests > Operator controlled PLMN selector handling > UE recognising the priority order of the Operator controlled PLMN selector list using the ACT preference - E-UTRAN in NB-S1/ E-UTRAN in WB-S1 mode

Title Path: PLMN related tests > Higher priority PLMN search handling > UE recognising the search period of the Higher priority PLMN > Method of test > Initial conditions
Content: For this test an UTRAN USS (in case of a Terminal accessing UTRAN) or a SS (in case of Terminal accessing a GERAN) is needed. After the registration of UE the USS (in case of a Terminal accessing UTRAN) or a SS (in case of Terminal accessing a GERAN) transmits on a second BCCH, with the following network parameters: Attach/detach: disabled. LAI (MCC/MNC/LAC): 244/081/0001. - RAI (MCC/MNC/LAC/RAC): 244/081/0001/05. (only for UTRAN cell) - Access control: unrestricted. NOTE: In case of a GERAN no packet system information is transmitted The default UICC shall be used with the following exception: EF (Higher Priority PLMN Search period) Logically: set to 6 minutes The UICC shall be installed into the Terminal and the UE shall be set to automatic PLMN selection mode. In case of a Terminal accessing UTRAN "Expected Sequence A" and in case of a Terminal accessing a GERAN "Expected Sequence B" shall be performed.

Title Path: Subscription independent tests > Phone book procedures > Recognition of a previously changed phonebook > Definition and applicability
Content: If the UICC is inserted into a GERAN Rel-4 or earlier terminal, the phonebook may have been altered in this GSM session. If the ADN entry has been changed or deleted, the GSM terminal will not be able to change the appropriate additional phonebook entries (e.g. EF Additional Number). In that case the UICC shall set a flag in the appropriate EF (phonebook Control). If the UICC is inserted in a 3G or GERAN Terminal, the 3G or GERAN Terminal shall recognise the flag and the phonebook shall be synchronised by the Terminal. Once the Terminal recognise the set flag in the EF , the Terminal shall update the Change Counter in the EF .
Title Path: Subscription independent tests > Phone book procedures > Recognition of a previously changed phonebook > Conformance requirement
Content: The 3G or GERAN Terminal shall recognise the set flag in the EF and then synchronise the phonebook. The Terminal shall also update EF (Change Counter). - TS 31.102 , clause 4.4.2.

Title Path: Subscription independent tests > Phone book procedures > Update of the Phonebook Synchronisation Counter (PSC) > Definition and applicability
Content: The phonebook synchronisation Counter is used to unambiguously identify the status of the phonebook. Every time the phonebook is reset/deleted or the UID and/or the CC has run out of range, the PSC shall be regenerated. The PSC is a part of the phonebook identifier.
Title Path: Subscription independent tests > Phone book procedures > Update of the Phonebook Synchronisation Counter (PSC) > Conformance requirement
Content: Every time either the UID or the CC is incremented by the Terminal, the value of the contend of the appropriate EF shall be tested. If either UID or CC has reached "FF FF", the related EF shall be set to "00 01" and the PSC is incremented. - TS 31.102 , clause 4.4.2.12.2.
Title Path: Subscription independent tests > Phone book procedures > Update of the Phonebook Synchronisation Counter (PSC) > Test purpose

Title Path: Subscription independent tests > Phone book procedures > Phonebook content handling > Handling of BCD number/ SSC content extension > Definition and applicability
Content: The length of BCD number/SSC contents in EF byte gives the number of bytes of the following two data items containing actual BCD number/SSC information. This means that the maximum value is 11, even when the actual ADN/SSC information length is greater than 11. When an ADN/SSC has extension, it is indicated by the extension1 identifier being unequal to 'FF'. The remainder is stored in the EF with the remaining length of the additional data being coded in the appropriate additional record itself.
Title Path: Subscription independent tests > Phone book procedures > Phonebook content handling > Handling of BCD number/ SSC content extension > Conformance requirement
Content: The terminal shall support the BCD number/ SSC extension for EF as defined in TS 31.102 , clauses 4.4.2.3 and 4.4.2.4. Reference: - TS 31.102 , clauses 4.4.2.3 and 4.4.2.4.

Title Path: records, each record non-empty and unique. Unless otherwise stated, the ADN records shall not use extended BCD numbers/SSC strings. > Acceptance criteria
Content: After step a) the terminal shall have activated the USIM application. After step b) the terminal shall have selected the global phonebook and shall have read EF in the global phonebook. After step c) the global phonebook shall contain a record with "22446622446622446600" as BCD number and "04" as extension record identifier. EF shall contain a record with "Additional data" as record type, the BCD number extension "777888999" and "FF" as identifier to indicate the end of the chain. After step f) the record of EF which was used to store the BCD number extension "777888999" shall be empty and the record used for storing the entry with the alpha identifier "Contact002" of EF shall contain the BCD number "22446622446600" and the extension record identifier "FF". After step g) a record of EF shall contain "NewContact" as alpha identifier, "12345678901234567890" as BCD number and shall use an extension record identifier unequal to "FF". If the maximum number of BCD digits supported for global phonebook updating is less than the requested input BCD number, then EF and EF shall contain the BCD number as entered on the MMI. After step h) the record of EF which was used to store the data for "Contact003" and the related records of EF shall be empty.
Title Path: records, each record non-empty and unique. Unless otherwise stated, the ADN records shall not use extended BCD numbers/SSC strings. > Phonebook selection > Definition and applicability
Content: The UICC may contain a global phonebook, or application specific phonebooks, or both in parallel. When both phonebook types co-exist, they are independent and no data is shared. In this case, it shall be possible for the user to select which phonebook the user would like to access.

Content: The terminal shall support the global and the application specific phonebooks as defined in TS 31.102 , clause 4.4.2. Reference: - TS 31.102 , clause 4.4.2.
Title Path: records, each record non-empty and unique. Unless otherwise stated, the ADN records shall not use extended BCD numbers/SSC strings. > Phonebook selection > Test purpose

After step i) the terminal shall have given an indication that update of the local phonebook can't be performed. EF shall have not been updated. After step j) the local phonebook record which was used to store the entry "Contact004" shall be empty and the terminal shall have indicated that the deletion of the phonebook entry was performed successfully. Content: An MMS User Agent shall use the MMS related information stored in the USIM, if present, unless otherwise specified by the user. Content: An MMS User Agent shall use the MMS related information stored in the USIM, if present, unless otherwise specified by the user. This information comprises MMS connectivity information, MMS user preferences and MMS notifications. MMS user preferences information, which is stored on the USIM, shall be used by an MMS User Agent for user assistance in preparation of terminal-originated MMs (e.g. default values for parameters that are often used).

Title Path: records, each record non-empty and unique. Unless otherwise stated, the ADN records shall not use extended BCD numbers/SSC strings. > MMS related tests > Usage of MMS notification > Method of test > Procedure
Content: [ a) ] The terminal is powered on and the PIN shall be entered. When the terminal is in idle mode a MM shall be sent to the terminal via the MMS Relay/Server 1 or 2, dependent on the bearer supported by the terminal. This MMS Relay/Server shall then generate a notification to the Terminal's MMS User Agent. With the MM notification the MMS User Agent shall receive a message reference that can be used for retrieving the MM from this MMS Relay/Server. The MM shall result in a MMS notification with the following predefined values: [X-Mms Message Type:]"m-notification-ind" (0x82) [X-Mms-Transaction-ID:]"01" [ X-Mms-MMS-Version: ]"1.0" [From:]not present (hidden) [Subject:]"MM for you" [X-Mms-Content-Location:]" [ a) ] The user shall read the MMS notification stored on the USIM. The user shall retrieve the MM stored on the MMS Relay/Server used in step b). The user shall forward the MM to "+0123456789" using the default MMS Issuer Connectivity Parameters stored on the USIM. A MM shall be sent to the terminal via the same MMS Relay/Server as in step b). This MMS Relay/Server shall then generate a notification to the Terminal's MMS User Agent. With the MM notification the MMS User Agent shall receive a message reference that can be used for retrieving the MM from this MMS Relay/Server. The MM shall result in a MMS notification with the following predefined values: [X-Mms Message Type:]"m-notification-ind" (0x82) [X-Mms-Transaction-ID:]"02" [ X-Mms-MMS-Version: ]"1.0" [From:]"+0987123654" [Subject:]"Urgent MM" [X-Mms-Content-Location:]" [ a) ] The user shall read the MMS notification stored on the USIM. The user shall reject the MM stored on the MMS Relay/Server used in step b).

Content: After step b) the MMS User Agent on the terminal shall have stored the MMS notification on the USIM with the values defined in step b) of 8.4.4.4.2, the associated status shall have been set to "Used space, notification not read, MM not retrieved" and the MMS User Agent shall indicate to the user that a MMS notification has been received. After step c) the status of the MMS notification stored on the USIM shall have been set to "used space, notification read, MM not retrieved". After step d) the MMS user agent shall have retrieved the MM from the MMS Relay/Server 1 and the status of the MMS notification stored on the USIM shall have either been set to "used space, notification read, MM retrieved" or the MMS notification shall have been deleted and the associated shall have been set to "Free space". After step e) the terminal shall have read the set of MMS Issuer Connectivity Parameters stored first in EF and shall have forward the MM to "+0123456789" using the MMS Relay/Server 1. The MMS notification shall have either been set to "used space, notification read, MM forwarded" or the MMS notification shall have been deleted and the associated shall have been set to "Free space". After step f) the MMS User Agent on the terminal shall have stored the MMS notification on the USIM with the values defined in step f) of 8.4.4.4.2, the associated status shall have been set to "Used space, notification not read, MM not retrieved" and the MMS User Agent shall indicate to the user that a MMS notification has been received. After step g) the status of the MMS notification stored on the USIM shall have been set to "used space, notification read, MM not retrieved". After step h) the MMS user agent shall have not retrieved the MM from the MMS Relay/Server 1 and the status of the MMS notification stored on the USIM shall have either been set to "used space, notification read, MM rejected" or the MMS notification shall have been deleted and the associated shall have been set to "Free space".
Title Path: records, each record non-empty and unique. Unless otherwise stated, the ADN records shall not use extended BCD numbers/SSC strings. > UICC presence detection > Definition and applicability
Content: To ensure that the UICC has not been removed during a card session, the Terminal sends in case of inactivity on the UICC-Terminal interface, at frequent intervals, a STATUS command during each call. This procedure shall be used in addition to a mechanical or other devices used to detect the removal of a UICC.
Title Path: records, each record non-empty and unique. Unless otherwise stated, the ADN records shall not use extended BCD numbers/SSC strings. > UICC presence detection > Conformance requirement
Content: A STATUS command shall be issued within all 30 second periods of inactivity on the UICC-Terminal interface during a call. Inactivity in this case is defined as starting at the end of the last communication or the last issued STATUS command. If no response data is received to this STATUS command, then the call shall be terminated as soon as possible but at least within 5s after the STATUS command has been sent. If the DF indicated in response to a STATUS command is not the same as that which was indicated in the previous response , or accessed by the previous command, then the call shall be terminated as soon as possible but at least within 5 seconds after the response data has been received. Here a call covers a circuit switched call, and/or an active PDP context. The ME may suspend the UICC presence detection based on STATUS commands in case it has an active PDP context, but has not exchanged any data with the network within a 30s period of inactivity on the UICC-ME interface, and resume it as soon as data is exchanged with the network, sending immediately a new STATUS command. TS 31.102 , clauses 5.1.9 ETSI TS 102 221 , clause 14.5.2.
Title Path: records, each record non-empty and unique. Unless otherwise stated, the ADN records shall not use extended BCD numbers/SSC strings. > UICC presence detection > Test purpose
Content: To verify that there are no periods of inactivity on the UICC Terminal interface greater than 30 seconds during a call. To verify that the terminal terminates a call within 5 s at the latest after having received an invalid response to the STATUS command.
Title Path: records, each record non-empty and unique. Unless otherwise stated, the ADN records shall not use extended BCD numbers/SSC strings. > UICC presence detection > Method of test > Initial conditions
Content: The terminal shall be connected to the UICC simulator. All elementary files shall be coded as default.

[ a) ] The UICC simulator shall monitor the time of periods of inactivity on the UICC-Terminal interface. After 3 minutes, the call or PDP context shall be cleared. A call shall be set up using the generic call setup for circuit switched call or to activate a PDP context . NOTE: In case of PDP context for a terminal that supports Rel-12 or later, exchange of data with the network may be required to guarantee the correct result of the test. e) After one minute after the call was successfully set up, the UICC simulator shall respond to a STATUS command with the response data indicating a DF different from the current DF.

Content: A STATUS command shall be issued within all 30 second periods of inactivity on the UICC-Terminal interface during an active PDP context. There is 1:1 mapping between one PDP context and one EPS Bearer. TS 31.102 , clauses 5.1.9 ETSI TS 102 221 , clause 14.5.2. - TS 23.060 , clause 9.2.1A.

Title Path: USIM service handling > Access Point Name Control List handling > Access Point Name Control List handling for terminals supporting ACL > Method of test > Procedure
Content: [ a) ] The terminal is switched on and the USIM application shall be activated. The user shall request a PDP context activation to "1gpp.test". The user shall request a PDP context activation to "3gpp.test". The user shall deactivate the PDP context. The user shall disable the APN Control List service. When prompted to enter PIN2, the user shall present the correct PIN2 value. The user shall request a PDP context activation to "1gpp.test". The user shall deactivate the PDP context and shall switch the terminal off and then switch on again. The user shall enable the APN Control List service. When prompted to enter PIN2, the user shall present the correct PIN2 value. The user shall request a PDP context activation to "1ppp.net". The terminal is switched off and on. The user shall add the APN "1ppp.net" to the APN Control List. When prompted to enter PIN2, the user shall present the correct PIN2 value. The user shall request a PDP context activation to "1ppp.net". The user shall deactivate the PDP context and switch off the terminal.
Title Path: USIM service handling > Access Point Name Control List handling > Access Point Name Control List handling for terminals supporting ACL > Acceptance criteria
Content: After step a) the terminal shall have activated the USIM application, shall have read the status of the ACL service in EF and EF and be in updated idle mode on the (U)SS. The terminal shall have not requested a PDP context activation in step b). After step c) the PDP context shall have been activated. After step d) the PDP context shall have been deactivated. After step e) the APN Control List service shall have been set to disabled in EF . After step f) the PDP context shall have been activated. After step g) the PDP context shall have been deactivated. After step h) the APN Control List service shall have been set to enabled in EF . The terminal shall not have requested a PDP context activation in step i). After step k) the APN "1ppp.net" shall have been added to the APN Control List in EF . After step l) the PDP context shall have been activated.

Title Path: CSG list handling > CSG list handling for E-UTRA > Automatic CSG selection in E-UTRA with CSG list on USIM, success > Definition and applicability
Content: A Closed Subscriber Group identifies subscribers of an operator who are permitted to access one or more cells of the PLMN but which have restricted access (CSG cells). A CSG cell is part of the PLMN, broadcasting a CSG indication that is set to TRUE and a specific CSG identity. A CSG cell is accessible by the members of the closed subscriber group for that CSG identity. For a CSG cell, the UE shall check the broadcast CSG ID against the Allowed CSG list provided by NAS to check whether a CSG cell is suitable for the UE.
Title Path: CSG list handling > CSG list handling for E-UTRA > Automatic CSG selection in E-UTRA with CSG list on USIM, success > Conformance requirement
Content: When a UE in idle mode detects the presence of a permissible CSG cell (a CSG cell whose CSG identity is in the UE's permitted CSG list), the UE shall select the CSG cell. The ME shall read the allowed CSG IDs from EF in order to perform HNB selection procedures. The lists in EF shall take precedence over the list stored in the ME non-volatile memory. If the MS supports CSG, it is provisioned with a list of allowed CSG identities and associated PLMN identities from the USIM if the list is available in the USIM. TS 22.011 , clause 8.2.2.1; TS 31.102 , clauses 4.4.6.2 and 5.8.1; TS 23.122 , clause 3.1A.
Title Path: CSG list handling > CSG list handling for E-UTRA > Automatic CSG selection in E-UTRA with CSG list on USIM, success > Test purpose
Content: To verify that the ME only selects a CSG cell if the CSG IDs of the cell is found in the allowed CSG IDs from EF
Title Path: CSG list handling > CSG list handling for E-UTRA > Automatic CSG selection in E-UTRA with CSG list on USIM, success > Method of test > Initial conditions
Content: For this test an E-USS is required. The E-USS transmits on two cells, with the following network parameters: TAI (MCC/MNC/TAC): 246/081/0001. Access control: unrestricted. csg-Indication: TRUE csg-Identity: 05 TAI (MCC/MNC/TAC): 246/081/0002. Access control: unrestricted. csg-Indication: TRUE csg-Identity: 04 The default E-UTRAN UICC is used. The UICC is installed into the Terminal and the UE is set to automatic PLMN selection mode.
Title Path: CSG list handling > CSG list handling for E-UTRA > Automatic CSG selection in E-UTRA with CSG list on USIM, success > Method of test > Procedure
Content: [ a) ] The UE is powered on. After 2 minutes the E-USS stops all RF output for the first cell with TAI 246/081/0001 on the BCCH for a long enough period of time to cause a cell reselection procedure in the UE. The BCCH is changed to contain: - csg-Identity: 03 The E-USS then resumes RF output on the BCCH. [ a) ] After receipt of an RRCConnectionRequest from the UE on the E-UTRAN-cell related to the BCCH transmitting TAI 246/081/0001, the E-USS sends RRCConnectionSetup to the UE, followed by RRCConnectionSetupComplete sent by the UE to the E-USS. During registration and after receipt of a AttachRequest from the UE, the E-USS initiates authentication, starts integrity by using the security procedure and sends AttachAccept with to the UE: [] TAI (MCC/MNC/TAC): 246/081/ 0001 [] GUTI: "24608100010266436587" After receipt of the AttachComplete during registration from the UE, the E-USS sends RRCConnectionRelease to the UE. The UE is soft powered down.
Title Path: CSG list handling > CSG list handling for E-UTRA > Automatic CSG selection in E-UTRA with CSG list on USIM, success > Acceptance criteria
Content: After steps a) the terminal shall not attempt an Attach procedure. 2) After step b) the UE shall send an RRCConnectionRequest on the E-UTRAN-cell related to the BCCH transmitting TAI 246/081/0001 to the e-USS. During step c) the terminal shall send AttachRequest to the E-USS. After step d) the terminal shall respond with AttachComplete during registration. After step e) the USIM shall contain the following values: EF (EPS Information) [Logically:]GUTI: 24608100010266436587 []Last visited registered TAI: 246/081/0001 []EPS update status: updated
Title Path: CSG list handling > CSG list handling for E-UTRA > Automatic CSG selection in E-UTRA with CSG list on USIM, removal of CSG ID from the USIM > Definition and applicability
Content: A Closed Subscriber Group identifies subscribers of an operator who are permitted to access one or more cells of the PLMN but which have restricted access (CSG cells). A CSG cell is part of the PLMN, broadcasting a CSG indication that is set to TRUE and a specific CSG identity. A CSG cell is accessible by the members of the closed subscriber group for that CSG identity. For a CSG cell, the UE shall check the broadcast CSG ID against the Allowed CSG list provided by NAS to check whether a CSG cell is suitable for the UE.
Title Path: CSG list handling > CSG list handling for E-UTRA > Automatic CSG selection in E-UTRA with CSG list on USIM, removal of CSG ID from the USIM > Conformance requirement
Content: When a UE in idle mode detects the presence of a permissible CSG cell (a CSG cell whose CSG identity is in the UE's permitted CSG list), the UE shall select the CSG cell. The ME shall read the allowed CSG IDs from EF in order to perform HNB selection procedures. The lists in EF shall take precedence over the list stored in the ME non-volatile memory. If the MS supports CSG, it is provisioned with a list of allowed CSG identities and associated PLMN identities from the USIM if the list is available in the USIM. If the UE receives ATTACH REJECT with cause \#25 (Not authorized for this CSG) with integrity protection, the UE shall remove the CSG ID of the cell where the UE has sent the ATTACH REQUEST message from the Allowed CSG list. TS 22.011 , clause 8.2.2.1; TS 31.102 , clauses 4.4.6.2 and 5.8.1; TS 23.122 , clause 3.1A. TS 24.301 , clause 5.5.1.2.5
Title Path: CSG list handling > CSG list handling for E-UTRA > Automatic CSG selection in E-UTRA with CSG list on USIM, removal of CSG ID from the USIM > Test purpose
Content: To verify that the ME removes the CSG ID from the Allowed CSG list in EF in case this CSG ID belongs to the cell where the ME has sent the ATTACH REQUEST message which was rejected with cause \#25 by the E-USS.
Title Path: CSG list handling > CSG list handling for E-UTRA > Automatic CSG selection in E-UTRA with CSG list on USIM, removal of CSG ID from the USIM > Method of test > Initial conditions
Content: For this test an E-USS is required. The E-USS transmits on two cells, with the following network parameters: TAI (MCC/MNC/TAC): 246/081/0001. Access control: unrestricted. csg-Indication: TRUE csg-Identity: 03 TAI (MCC/MNC/TAC): 246/081/0002. Access control: unrestricted. csg-Indication: TRUE csg-Identity: 04 The default E-UTRAN UICC is used. The UICC is installed into the Terminal and the UE is set to automatic PLMN selection mode.
Title Path: CSG list handling > CSG list handling for E-UTRA > Automatic CSG selection in E-UTRA with CSG list on USIM, removal of CSG ID from the USIM > Method of test > Procedure
Content: [ a) ] The UE is powered on. After receipt of an RRCConnectionRequest from the UE on the E-UTRAN-cell related to the BCCH transmitting TAI 246/081/0001, the E-USS sends RRCConnectionSetup to the UE, followed by RRCConnectionSetupComplete sent by the UE to the E-USS. During registration and after receipt of an AttachRequest from the UE, the E-USS initiates authentication, starts integrity by using the security procedure and sends AttachReject to the UE with cause \#25 (Not authorized for this CSG) with integrity protection, followed by RRCConnectionRelease. The UE is soft powered down.
Title Path: CSG list handling > CSG list handling for E-UTRA > Automatic CSG selection in E-UTRA with CSG list on USIM, removal of CSG ID from the USIM > Acceptance criteria
Content: 1) After step a) the UE shall send an RRCConnectionRequest on the E-UTRAN-cell related to the BCCH transmitting TAI 246/081/0001 to the E-USS. During step b) the terminal shall send AttachRequest to the E-USS. After step c) the USIM shall contain the following values: EF (EPS Information) [Logically:]GUTI: not checked []Last visited registered TAI: 246/081/0001 []EPS update status: ROAMING NOT ALLOWED EF (Allowed CSG Lists) Logically: 1st CSG list []PLMN: 246 081 (MCC MNC) []1st CSG list 1st CSG Type indication 02 []1st CSG list 1st CSG HNB Name indication 02 []1st CSG list 1st CSG CSG ID: 02 (27bit) 2nd CSG list []PLMN: 244 081 (MCC MNC) []2nd CSG list 1st CSG Type indication 08 []2nd CSG list 1st CSG HNB Name indication 08 []2nd CSG list 1st CSG CSG ID: 08 (27bit) Note: the 1st and 2nd CSG list may be stored together or separately in any record in arbitrary order.
Title Path: CSG list handling > CSG list handling for E-UTRA > Manual CSG selection in E-UTRA with CSG list on USIM, success > Definition and applicability
Content: A Closed Subscriber Group identifies subscribers of an operator who are permitted to access one or more cells of the PLMN but which have restricted access (CSG cells). A CSG cell is part of the PLMN, broadcasting a CSG indication that is set to TRUE and a specific CSG identity. A CSG cell is accessible by the members of the closed subscriber group for that CSG identity. For a CSG cell, the UE shall check the broadcast CSG ID against the Allowed CSG list provided by NAS to check whether a CSG cell is suitable for the UE. A UE supporting CSG selection selects CSG cell either automatically based on the list of allowed CSG identities or manually based on user selection of CSG on indication of list of available CSGs.
Title Path: CSG list handling > CSG list handling for E-UTRA > Manual CSG selection in E-UTRA with CSG list on USIM, success > Conformance requirement
Content: The ME shall read the allowed CSG IDs from EF in order to perform HNB selection procedures. The lists in EF shall take precedence over the list stored in the ME non-volatile memory. In manual CSG selection mode, the ME indicates to the user the list of available CSGs in the currently selected PLMN. The list of CSGs presented to the user is not restricted by the allowed CSG list. If the MS supports CSG, it is provisioned with a list of allowed CSG identities and associated PLMN identities from the USIM if the list is available in the USIM. If the UE supporting CSG selection has attempted manual CSG selection, the UE, when receiving the TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message, shall check if the CSG ID of the cell where the UE has sent the TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message is contained in the Allowed CSG list. If not, the UE shall add that CSG ID to the Allowed CSG list. TS 31.102 , clauses 4.4.6.2 and 5.8.1; TS 23.122 , clause 3.1A. TS 24.301 , clause 5.5.3.2.4
Title Path: CSG list handling > CSG list handling for E-UTRA > Manual CSG selection in E-UTRA with CSG list on USIM, success > Test purpose
Content: To verify that the ME adds the CSG ID to the Allowed CSG list in EF in case this CSG ID belongs to the cell where the ME has sent the TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message which was accepted by the E-USS.
Title Path: CSG list handling > CSG list handling for E-UTRA > Manual CSG selection in E-UTRA with CSG list on USIM, success > Method of test > Initial conditions

Title Path: CSG list handling > CSG list handling for E-UTRA > CSG selection in E-UTRA with no CSG list on USIM, no IMSI change > Definition and applicability
Content: A Closed Subscriber Group identifies subscribers of an operator who are permitted to access one or more cells of the PLMN but which have restricted access (CSG cells). A CSG cell is part of the PLMN, broadcasting a CSG indication that is set to TRUE and a specific CSG identity. A CSG cell is accessible by the members of the closed subscriber group for that CSG identity. Title Path: CSG list handling > CSG list handling for E-UTRA > CSG selection in E-UTRA with no CSG list on USIM, no IMSI change > Conformance requirement
Content: In manual CSG selection mode, the ME indicates to the user the list of available CSGs in the currently selected PLMN. The list of CSGs presented to the user is not restricted by the allowed CSG list. If the MS supports CSG, it is provisioned with a list of allowed CSG identities and associated PLMN identities from the USIM if the list is available in the USIM. If the UE supporting CSG selection has attempted manual CSG selection, the UE, when receiving the TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message, shall check if the CSG ID of the cell where the UE has sent the TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message is contained in the Allowed CSG list. If not, the UE shall add that CSG ID to the Allowed CSG list. If the corresponding file is not present on the USIM, these EMM parameters except allowed CSG list are stored in a non-volatile memory in the ME together with the IMSI from the USIM. The allowed CSG list is stored in a non-volatile memory in the ME if the UE supports CSG selection. These EMM parameters can only be used if the IMSI from the USIM matches the IMSI stored in the non-volatile memory; else the UE shall delete the EMM parameters. TS 31.102 , clauses 4.4.6.2 and 5.8.1; TS 23.122 , clause 3.1A. TS 24.301 , clause 5.5.3.2.4 and Annex C.
Title Path: CSG list handling > CSG list handling for E-UTRA > CSG selection in E-UTRA with no CSG list on USIM, no IMSI change > Test purpose
Content: To verify that the ME adds the CSG ID to the Allowed CSG list in a non-volatile memory in the ME together with the IMSI from the USIM in case this CSG ID belongs to the cell where the ME has sent the TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message which was accepted by the E-USS as the corresponding file is not present on the simulated USIM. To verify that the ME still has this CSG ID stored in the Allowed CSG list available together with the IMSI after powered down and up in case the IMSI of the USIM has not changed. To verify that the ME removes the CSG ID from the Allowed CSG list inside the terminal in case this CSG ID belongs to the cell where the ME has sent the ATTACH REQUEST message which was rejected with cause \#25 by the E-USS.

A CSG cell is accessible by the members of the closed subscriber group for that CSG identity. For a CSG cell, the UE shall check the broadcast CSG ID against the Allowed CSG list provided by NAS to check whether a CSG cell is suitable for the UE. A UE supporting CSG selection selects CSG cell either automatically based on the list of allowed CSG identities or manually based on user selection of CSG on indication of list of available CSGs.
Title Path: CSG list handling > CSG list handling for E-UTRA > CSG selection in E-UTRA with no CSG list on USIM, with IMSI change > Conformance requirement
Content: In manual CSG selection mode, the ME indicates to the user the list of available CSGs in the currently selected PLMN. The list of CSGs presented to the user is not restricted by the allowed CSG list.. If the MS supports CSG, it is provisioned with a list of allowed CSG identities and associated PLMN identities from the USIM if the list is available in the USIM. If the UE supporting CSG selection has attempted manual CSG selection, the UE, when receiving the TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message, shall check if the CSG ID of the cell where the UE has sent the TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message is contained in the Allowed CSG list. If not, the UE shall add that CSG ID to the Allowed CSG list. If the corresponding file is not present on the USIM, these EMM parameters except allowed CSG list are stored in a non-volatile memory in the ME together with the IMSI from the USIM. The allowed CSG list is stored in a non-volatile memory in the ME if the UE supports CSG selection. These EMM parameters can only be used if the IMSI from the USIM matches the IMSI stored in the non-volatile memory; else the UE shall delete the EMM parameters. TS 31.102 , clauses 4.4.6.2 and 5.8.1; TS 23.122 , clause 3.1A. TS 24.301 , clause 5.5.3.2.4 and Annex C.
Title Path: CSG list handling > CSG list handling for E-UTRA > CSG selection in E-UTRA with no CSG list on USIM, with IMSI change > Test purpose
Content: To verify that the ME adds the CSG ID to the Allowed CSG list in a non-volatile memory in the ME together with the IMSI from the USIM in case this CSG ID belongs to the cell where the ME has sent the TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message which was accepted by the E-USS as the corresponding file is not present on the simulated USIM. To verify that the ME removes this CSG ID stored in the Allowed CSG list available together with the IMSI after powered down and up in case the IMSI of the USIM has changed.
Title Path: CSG list handling > CSG list handling for E-UTRA > CSG selection in E-UTRA with no CSG list on USIM, with IMSI change > Method of test > Initial conditions
Content: For this test an E-USS is required. The E-USS transmits on two cells, with the following network parameters: TAI (MCC/MNC/TAC): 246/081/0001. Access control: unrestricted. csg-Indication: FALSE csg-Identity: not present TAI (MCC/MNC/TAC): 246/081/0002. Access control: unrestricted. csg-Indication: TRUE csg-Identity: 04 The default UICC (without the service "Allowed CSG Lists and corresponding indications") is installed into the Terminal. The ME shall not have csg-ID = 04 nor csg-ID=06 in the allowed CSG list stored in a non-volatile memory in the ME and the ME is set to automatic PLMN selection mode.
Title Path: CSG list handling > CSG list handling for E-UTRA > CSG selection in E-UTRA with no CSG list on USIM, with IMSI change > Method of test > Procedure
Content: [ a) ] The UE is powered on. After receipt of an RRCConnectionRequest from the UE on the E-UTRAN-cell related to the BCCH transmitting TAI 246/081/0001, the E-USS sends RRCConnectionSetup to the UE, followed by RRCConnectionSetupComplete sent by the UE to the E-USS. During registration and after receipt of an AttachRequest from the UE, the E-USS initiates authentication, starts integrity by using the security procedure and sends AttachAccept with to the following parameters the UE: [] TAI (MCC/MNC/TAC): 246/081/ 0001 [] GUTI: "24608100010266345678" After receipt of the AttachComplete during registration from the UE, the E-USS sends RRCConnectionRelease to the UE. The MMI of the UE is used to perform manual CSG selection. The UE shall indicate the availability of a cell with csg-Identity 04 for PLMN 246/081. The user shall select this cell by using the MMI. After receipt of an RRCConnectionRequest from the UE on the E-UTRAN-cell related to the BCCH transmitting TAI 246/081/0002, the E-USS sends RRCConnectionSetup to the UE, followed by RRCConnectionSetupComplete sent by the UE to the E-USS. During registration and after receipt of a TrackingAreaUpdateRequest from the UE, the E-USS may initiate authentication, may start integrity by using the security procedure and sends TrackingAreaUpdateAccept with the following parameters to the UE: [] TAI (MCC/MNC/TAC): 246/081/ 0002 [] GUTI: "24608100010266345699" After receipt of the TrackingAreaUpdateComplete during registration from the UE, the E-USS sends RRCConnectionRelease to the UE. The UE is switched off and performs the Detach procedure. A new UICC with the following configuration is activated: The default UICC with the following exception: The IMSI is set to "246081222233333". The E-USS shall change the BCCH for the cell transmitting TAI 246/081/0001 to the following network parameters: []- csg-Indication: TRUE []- csg-Identity: 06 [ a) ] The UE is powered on. After 2 minutes the UE is soft powered down.

Title Path: CSG list handling > CSG list handling for E-UTRA > Manual CSG selection without display restrictions in E-UTRA with ACSG list and OCSG list on USIM > Definition and applicability
Content: A Closed Subscriber Group identifies subscribers of an operator who are permitted to access one or more cells of the PLMN but which have restricted access (CSG cells). A CSG cell is part of the PLMN, broadcasting a CSG indication that is set to TRUE and a specific CSG identity. A CSG cell is accessible by the members of the closed subscriber group for that CSG identity. For a CSG cell, the UE shall check the broadcast CSG ID against the Allowed CSG list provided by NAS to check whether a CSG cell is suitable for the UE. A UE supporting CSG selection selects a CSG cell either automatically based on the list of allowed CSG identities or manually based on user selection of CSG on indication of list of available CSGs. Editor's note: it is still being investigated whether the testing of Automatic CSG selection should be performed using a separate test case or an enhanced version of the Manual CSG selection test case.
Title Path: CSG list handling > CSG list handling for E-UTRA > Manual CSG selection without display restrictions in E-UTRA with ACSG list and OCSG list on USIM > Conformance requirement
Content: The ME shall read the allowed CSG IDs from EF and EF in order to perform HNB selection procedures. The lists in EF and EF shall take precedence over the list stored in the ME non-volatile memory. If the MS supports CSG, it is provisioned with a list of allowed CSG identities and associated PLMN identities from the USIM if the list is available in the USIM. If the UE supporting CSG selection has attempted manual CSG selection, the UE, when receiving the TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message, shall check if the CSG ID of the cell where the UE has sent the TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message is contained in the Allowed CSG list. If not, the UE shall add that CSG ID to the Allowed CSG list EF . By default, the UE shall display all available CSGs for any PLMN, unless the UE has been configured by the HPLMN, for a specific PLMN, to display only CSGs in the Operator CSG List that are available. TS 31.102 , clauses 4.2.18, 4.4.6.2, 4.4.6.5 and 5.8.1; TS 24.301 , clause 5.5.3.2.4 TS 22.220 , clause 5.3.2 and 5.5.4
Title Path: CSG list handling > CSG list handling for E-UTRA > Manual CSG selection without display restrictions in E-UTRA with ACSG list and OCSG list on USIM > Test purpose

The lists in EF and EF shall take precedence over the list stored in the ME non-volatile memory. If the MS supports CSG, it is provisioned with a list of allowed CSG identities and associated PLMN identities from the USIM if the list is available in the USIM. If the UE supporting CSG selection has attempted manual CSG selection, the UE, when receiving the ROUTING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message, shall check if the CSG ID of the cell where the UE has sent the ROUTING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message is contained in the Allowed CSG list. If not, the UE shall add that CSG ID to the Allowed CSG list EF . By default, the UE shall display all available CSGs for any PLMN, unless the UE has been configured by the HPLMN, for a specific PLMN, to display only CSGs in the Operator CSG List that are available. TS 31.102 , clauses 4.2.18, 4.4.6.2, 4.4.6.5 and 5.8.1; TS 23.122 , clause 3.1A. TS 22.220 , clause 5.3.2 and 5.5.4
Title Path: CSG list handling > CSG list handling for UTRA > Manual CSG selection with display restrictions in UTRA with ACSG list and OCSG list on USIM > Test purpose
Content: To verify that the ME adds the CSG ID to the Allowed CSG list in EF in case this CSG ID belongs to the cell where the ME has sent the ROUTING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message which was accepted by the USS. During the manual CSG selection all available CSG ID shall be displayed with restrictions.

Title Path: CSG list handling > CSG list handling for UTRA > Manual CSG selection with display restrictions in UTRA with ACSG list and OCSG list on USIM > Method of test > Procedure
Content: [ a) ] The UE is powered on. After receipt of an RRCConnectionRequest from the UE on the UTRAN-cell related to the BCCH transmitting R AI 246/081/0001/01, the USS sends RRCConnectionSetup to the UE, followed by RRCConnectionSetupComplete sent by the UE to the USS. During registration and after receipt of an AttachRequest from the UE, the USS initiates authentication, starts integrity by using the security procedure and sends AttachAccept with to the UE: [] RAI (MCC/MNC/LAC/RAC): 246/081/0001/01 [] P-TMSI "87512890" After receipt of the AttachComplete during registration from the UE, the USS sends RRCConnectionRelease to the UE. The MMI of the UE is used to perform manual CSG selection. The UE shall not indicate the availability of a cell with csg-Identity 04 for PLMN 246/080, this shall be verified for 2 minutes. The USS stops all RF output for the first cell with R AI 246/081/0001/01 on the BCCH. The BCCH is changed to contain: RAI (MCC/MNC/LAC/RAC): 246/081/0002/02. - csg-Indication: TRUE - csg-Identity: 04 The USS then resumes RF output on the BCCH. The MMI of the UE is used to perform manual CSG selection. The UE shall indicate the availability of a cell with csg-Identity 04 for PLMN 246/081. The user shall select this cell by using the MMI. After receipt of an RRCConnectionRequest from the UE on the UTRAN-cell related to the BCCH transmitting R AI 246/081/0002/02, the USS sends RRCConnectionSetup to the UE, followed by RRCConnectionSetupComplete sent by the UE to the USS. During registration and after receipt of a Rout ingAreaUpdateRequest from the UE, the USS initiates authentication, starts integrity by using the security procedure and sends Routing AreaUpdateAccept with to the UE: [] RAI (MCC/MNC/TAC): 246/081/0002/02 [] P-TMSI "34567890" After receipt of the Routing AreaUpdatComplete during registration from the UE, the USS sends RRCConnectionRelease to the UE. The UE is soft powered down.

Title Path: CSG list handling > CSG list handling for UTRA > Manual CSG selection in UTRA with CSG list on USIM, success > Definition and applicability
Content: A Closed Subscriber Group identifies subscribers of an operator who are permitted to access one or more cells of the PLMN but which have restricted access (CSG cells). A CSG cell is part of the PLMN, broadcasting a CSG indication that is set to TRUE and a specific CSG identity. A CSG cell is accessible by the members of the closed subscriber group for that CSG identity. For a CSG cell, the UE shall check the broadcast CSG ID against the Allowed CSG list provided by NAS to check whether a CSG cell is suitable for the UE. A UE supporting CSG selection selects CSG cell either automatically based on the list of allowed CSG identities or manually based on user selection of CSG on indication of list of available CSGs. Editor's note: it is still being investigated whether the testing of both the unsuccessful Manual CSG selection and the Automatic CSG selection should be performed using a separate test case or an enhanced version of the Manual CSG selection test case.
Title Path: CSG list handling > CSG list handling for UTRA > Manual CSG selection in UTRA with CSG list on USIM, success > Conformance requirement
Content: The ME shall read the allowed CSG IDs from EF in order to perform HNB selection procedures. The lists in EF shall take precedence over the list stored in the ME non-volatile memory. In manual CSG selection mode, the ME indicates to the user the list of available CSGs in the currently selected PLMN. The list of CSGs presented to the user is not restricted by the allowed CSG list. If the MS supports CSG, it is provisioned with a list of allowed CSG identities and associated PLMN identities from the USIM if the list is available in the USIM. If the UE supporting CSG selection has attempted manual CSG selection, the UE, when receiving the ROUTING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message, shall check if the CSG ID of the cell where the UE has sent the ROUTING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message is contained in the Allowed CSG list. If not, the UE shall add that CSG ID to the Allowed CSG list. TS 31.102 , clauses 4.4.6.2 and 5.8.1; TS 23.122 , clause 3.1A. TS 24.008 , clause 4.7.5.1.3
