Title Path: NAS security context parameter handling > NAS security context parameter handling when service "EMM Information" is available > Definition and applicability
Content: The security parameters for authentication, integrity protection and ciphering are tied together in an EPS security context and identified by a key set identifier for E-UTRAN (eKSI). The relationship between the security parameters is defined in 3GPP TS 33.401 . The EPS security context parameters shall be stored on the USIM if the corresponding file is present. If the corresponding file is not present on the USIM, these EMM parameters except allowed CSG list are stored in a non-volatile memory in the ME together with the IMSI from the USIM. The EF contains the EPS NAS Security context as defined in TS 33.401 . This file shall contain only one record and shall be updated only when the requirements defined in TS 33.401 are met.
Title Path: NAS security context parameter handling > NAS security context parameter handling when service "EMM Information" is available > Conformance requirement
Content: EPS AKA is the authentication and key agreement procedure that shall be used over E-UTRAN. Before security can be activated, the MME and the UE need to establish an EPS security context. Usually, the EPS security context is created as the result of an authentication procedure between MME and UE. The EPS security context parameters shall be stored on the USIM if the corresponding file is present, and shall be updated only when the requirements defined in TS 33.401 are met. If the corresponding file is not present on the USIM, these EMM parameters except allowed CSG list are stored in a non-volatile memory in the ME together with the IMSI from the USIM. TS 24.301 , clause 4.4.2.1 and Annex C; TS 31.102 , clause 4.2.92; TS 33.401 , clause 6.1.1, 7.2.5.1 and 7.2.5.2.1.
Title Path: NAS security context parameter handling > NAS security context parameter handling when service "EMM Information" is available > Test purpose
Content: To verify that the ME generates the EPS security context identified by a key set identifier for E-UTRAN (eKSI) and stores all inside EF if this EF is available and when the requirements defined in TS 33.401 , clauses 7.2.5.1 and 7.2.5.2.1 are met.

Title Path: NAS security context parameter handling > NAS security context parameter handling when service "EMM Information" is available > Method of test > Procedure
Content: [ a) ] The UE is switched on. After receipt of an RRCConnectionRequest/RRCConnectionRequest-NB from the UE the E-USS/NB-SS sends RRCConnectionSetup/RRCConnectionSetup-NB to the UE, followed by RRCConnectionSetupComplete/RRCConnectionSetupComplete-NB sent by the UE to the E-USS/NB-SS. Title Path: NAS security context parameter handling > NAS security context parameter handling when service "EMM Information" is available > Acceptance criteria
Content: After step a) the UE shall read EF and EF . During step b) the UE shall indicate in the AttachRequest that no key is available. During step c) the UE shall send the AuthenticationResponse message. During step d) the UE shall send the (NAS) SecurityModeComplete message. EF shall not be updated during steps c) to e), unless for invalidating the content of EF . Note: Invalidation of EF is described in TS 31.102 , clause 4.2.92. After step f) the UE shall send DETACH REQUEST to the E-USS/NB-SS. After step f) EF shall contain: EF (EPS NAS Security Context) Logically: Key Set Identifier KSI : '00' ASME Key (KSI ): 32 byte key, value not checked Uplink NAS count: any value Downlink NAS count: any value Identifiers of selected NAS any value integrity and encryption algorithm

Title Path: NAS security context parameter handling > EPS NAS Security Context Storage > Conformance requirement
Content: EPS AKA is the authentication and key agreement procedure that shall be used over E-UTRAN. Before security can be activated, the MME and the UE need to establish an EPS security context. Usually, the EPS security context is created as the result of an authentication procedure between MME and UE. The EPS security context parameters shall be stored on the USIM if the corresponding file is present, and shall be updated only when the requirements defined in TS 33.401 are met. TS 24.301 , clause 4.4.2.1 and Annex C; TS 31.102 , clause 4.2.92 and 5.2.28; TS 33.401 , clause 6.1.1, 7.2.5.2, 7.2.6.1 and 7.2.6.3.

Content: The update of EPS NAS security context shall be according to the rules and procedures specified in TS 33.401 , clause 6.1.1, 7.2.5.2, 7.2.6.1 and 7.2.6.3.

Title Path: Non Access Stratum (NAS) Configuration parameter handling > EF NAS signaling priority handling > Definition and applicability
Content: If the UE is configured for NAS signalling priority (see 3GPP TS 24.368 , 3GPP TS 31.102 ), the UE shall indicate this by including the Device properties IE in the appropriate NAS message and setting the low priority indicator to "MS is configured to NAS signalling low priority". This NAS signalling low priority indication can be used by the network for NAS level mobility management congestion control on a per core network node basis and APN based congestion control. The test case is covered in TS 34.123-1 clauses 9.4.3.7, 9.4.5.5, 11.1.1.3, 11.1.1.4, 11.1.3.4, 11.2.2.3, 12.4.1.1e and 12.4.3.2a. Refer to CR \#0229 for details.
Title Path: Non Access Stratum (NAS) Configuration parameter handling > EF NMO I Network Mode of Operation I handling > Definition and applicability
Content: The behaviour of the UE with respect to NMO I is determined by the combination of PS domain specific system information IE and the setting of the parameter "NMO_I_Behaviour" in the NAS configuration Management Object as specified in 3GPP TS 24.368 or in USIM file NASCONFIG as specified in 3GPP TS 31.102 . The test case is covered in TS 34.123-1 clause 12.2.2.3a. Refer to CR \#0230 for details.
Title Path: Non Access Stratum (NAS) Configuration parameter handling > EF Attach with IMSI handling > Definition and applicability
Content: The AttachWithIMSI leaf indicates whether attach with IMSI is performed when moving to a non-equivalent PLMN as specified in 3GPP TS 24.008 and 3GPP TS 24.301 . The test case is covered in TS 34.123-1 clause 12.2.1.1a. Refer to CR \#0224 for details.
Title Path: Non Access Stratum (NAS) Configuration parameter handling > EF Verifying Minimum Periodic Search Timer > Definition and applicability
Content: The MinimumPeriodicSearchTimer leaf gives a minimum value in minutes for the timer T controlling the periodic search for higher prioritized PLMNs as specified in 3GPP TS 23.122 . If the MS is configured for Fast First Higher Priority PLMN search and the MinimumPeriodicSearchTimer is configured as specified in 3GPP TS 24.368 or 3GPP TS 31.102 , the MS shall not use a value for T that is less than the MinimumPeriodicSearchTimer. The test case is covered in TS 34.123-1 clauses 9.4.5.4 and 9.4.5.4.7. Refer to CR \#0228 for details.
Title Path: Non Access Stratum (NAS) Configuration parameter handling > EF Extended access barring handling > Definition and applicability
Content: Extended Access Barring (EAB) is a mechanism to control Mobile Originating access attempts from UEs that are configures for EAB in order to prevent overload for the access network and/or the core network. In congestion situations, the operator can restrict access from UEs configured for EAB while permitting access from other UEs. The ExtendedAccessBarring leaf indicates whether the extended access barring is applicable for the UE as specified in 3GPP TS 24.008 and 3GPP TS 24.301 . The test case is covered in TS 34.123-1 clauses 8.1.1.20, 9.4.11, 12.2.1.16 and 12.4.1.9. Refer to CR \#0226 for details.
Title Path: Non Access Stratum (NAS) Configuration parameter handling > EF Verifying Timer T3245 Behaviour > Definition and applicability
Content: For an MS that is configured to use timer T3245 (see 3GPP TS 24.368 or 3GPP TS 31.102 ) and when the MS adds a PLMN identity to the "forbidden PLMN list" or the "forbidden PLMNs for GPRS service" list or sets the SIM/USIM as invalid for non-GPRS services or GPRS services or both, and timer T3245 is not running, the MS shall start timer T3245 with a random value, uniformly drawn from the range between 12h and 24h. Upon expiry of the timer T3245, the MS shall erase the "forbidden PLMN list" and the "forbidden PLMNs for GPRS service" list and set the SIM/USIM to valid for non-GPRS services and GPRS services.
Title Path: Non Access Stratum (NAS) Configuration parameter handling > EF Verifying Timer T3245 Behaviour > Conformance requirement
Content: For NAS configuration parameter by USIM, the UE shall check and apply the setting present in EF for "Timer T3245 Behaviour". Reference: TS 31.102 , clauses 4.2.94, 5.2.29 TS 24.368 , clause 5.7. TS 24.008 , clause 4.1.1.6

Title Path: Non Access Stratum (NAS) Configuration parameter handling > EF Verifying Timer T3245 Behaviour > Method of test > Procedure
Content: [ a) ] The UE is powered on. Depending on which domain the UE is going to be registered on, the UE attempts to perform CS, PS or CS/PS registration to the USS. Title Path: UICC interface during PSM > UICC interface in PSM handling for E-UTRAN No UICC deactivation in PSM > Definition and applicability
Content: PSM is intended for UEs that are expecting only infrequent mobile originating and terminating services and that can accept a corresponding latency in the mobile terminating communication. In order to reduce power consumption while in PSM, and only in case the PIN of the USIM is disabled, the ME may optionally deactivate the UICC after entering the PSM.
Title Path: UICC interface during PSM > UICC interface in PSM handling for E-UTRAN No UICC deactivation in PSM > Conformance requirement
Content: In order to reduce power consumption while the ME is in PSM, and only in case the PIN of the USIM is disabled, the ME may optionally deactivate the UICC (as specified in clause 6A.1 of 3GPP TS 31.101 ) after entering the PSM. Reference: TS 31.102 , clause 5.1.10; TS 24.301 , clauses 5.3.5 and 5.3.11. TS 31.101 , clause 6A.1.
Title Path: UICC interface during PSM > UICC interface in PSM handling for E-UTRAN No UICC deactivation in PSM > Test purpose
Content: 1) To verify that UE does not deactivate the UICC in case the PIN for the USIM is enabled and verified.
Title Path: UICC interface during PSM > UICC interface in PSM handling for E-UTRAN No UICC deactivation in PSM > Method of test > Initial conditions
Content: The UE is configured to use Power Saving Mode. The UE is configured to use the timer T3324 set to T3324_V. The E-USS transmits on the BCCH, with the following network parameters: TAI (MCC/MNC/TAC): 246/081/0001. Access control: unrestricted. The NB-SS transmits on the BCCH, with the following network parameters: TAI (MCC/MNC/TAC): 246/081/0001. Access control: unrestricted. The default E-UTRAN UICC is used with the following exceptions: EF (UICC Maximum Power Consumption) Logically: [UICC maximum power consumption:]60 mA [Operator defined time out (T_OP):]5 seconds [Additional information:]UICC does not require increased idle current []UICC does not support the UICC suspension procedure Byte 4 and byte 5: RFU The PIN of the USIM is enabled and verified
Title Path: UICC interface during PSM > UICC interface in PSM handling for E-UTRAN No UICC deactivation in PSM > Method of test > Procedure
Content: a) The UE is switched on. b) The UE requests RRC Connection and transmits an ATTACH REQUEST message to the E-USS/NB-SS including T3324 set to T3324_V. c) The E-USS/NB-SS sends the ATTACH ACCEPT message contains T3324 set to T3324_V and T3412 set to T3412_V.. It shall not contain the eDRX parameters d) After receipt of the AttachComplete during registration from the UE, the E-USS/NB-SS sends RRCConnectionRelease/RRCConnectionRelease-NB, to the UE. e) After the T3412 timer expires the UE sends TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST f) The E-USS/NB-SS sends TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT. g) The UE is switched off.
Title Path: UICC interface during PSM > UICC interface in PSM handling for E-UTRAN No UICC deactivation in PSM > Acceptance criteria
Content: 1) After step c) the UE shall not deactivate the UICC or send SUSPEND UICC command.

Title Path: UICC interface during PSM > UICC interface in PSM handling for E-UTRAN PSM not accepted by E-USS/NB-SS > Method of test > Procedure

Title Path: UICC interface during PSM > UICC interface in PSM handling for E-UTRAN UICC deactivation in PSM > Conformance requirement
Content: In order to reduce power consumption while the ME is in PSM, and only in case the PIN of the USIM is disabled, the ME may optionally deactivate the UICC (as specified in clause 6A.1 of 3GPP TS 31.101 ) after entering the PSM. In this case, the ME shall perform these steps before it can leave the PSM: - re-activate the UICC (as specified in clause 6A.1 of 3GPP TS 31.101 ), - re-initialize the USIM (as specified in clause 5.1.1 ), with the exception of re-reading EFs that are not required for the verification of the USIM, - take appropriate steps to verify that the same USIM is used. Verification shall include at least the check of the content of the following EFs: EF , EF and EF , and/or EF and/or EF (depending on which of these specific EFs containing LOCI the ME used prior to entering PSM) Reference: TS 31.102 , clause 5.1.10; TS 24.301 , clauses 5.3.5 and 5.3.11. TS 31.101 in clause 6A.1.

Title Path: UICC interface during PSM > UICC interface in PSM for E-UTRAN SUSPEND UICC > Definition and applicability
Content: PSM is intended for UEs that are expecting only infrequent mobile originating and terminating services and that can accept a corresponding latency in the mobile terminating communication. In this case, the ME shall successfully resume the UICC before it can leave the PSM. Reference: TS 31.102 , clause 5.1.10; TS 24.301 , clauses 5.3.5, 5.3.11 and 5.5.1.2.2. TS 31.101 in clause 11.1.22.

Title Path: UICC interface during PSM > UICC interface in PSM for E-UTRAN SUSPEND UICC > Method of test > Initial conditions
Content: The ME is configured to use Power Saving Mode. The ME is configured to use the timer T3324 set to T3324_V. The E-USS transmits on the BCCH, with the following network parameters: TAI (MCC/MNC/TAC): 246/081/0001. Access control: unrestricted. The NB-SS transmits on the BCCH, with the following network parameters: TAI (MCC/MNC/TAC): 246/081/0001. Access control: unrestricted. The default E-UTRAN UICC is used with the following exceptions: EF Logically: UICC maximum power consumption: 60 mA Operator defined time out (T_OP): 5 seconds Additional information: UICC does not require increased idle current UICC supports the UICC suspension procedure Byte 4 and byte 5: RFU The PIN of the USIM is enabled and verified.
Title Path: UICC interface during PSM > UICC interface in PSM for E-UTRAN SUSPEND UICC > Method of test > Procedure
Content: [ a) ] The UE is switched on. The UE requests RRC Connection and transmits an ATTACH REQUEST message to the E-USS/NB-SS including T3324 set to T3324_V. The E-USS/NB-SS sends the ATTACH ACCEPT message contains T3324 set to T3324_V and T3412 set to T3412_V. It shall not contain the eDRX parameters. After receipt of the AttachComplete during registration from the UE, the E-USS/NB-SS sends RRCConnectionRelease/RRCConnectionRelease-NB, to the UE. The ME sends SUSPEND UICC command to the UICC indicating "Minimum duration of the suspension proposed by the terminal" and the "Maximum duration of the suspension proposed by the terminal". The UICC returns a maximum suspension duration in the range proposed by the ME , Resume token and SW 9000. After the T3412 timer expires the UE sends TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST The E-USS/NB-SS sends TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT. The UE is switched off. NOTE: For testing purposes, and to not extend the test execution time the maximum suspension duration returned by the UICC shall be equal to the minimum duration of the suspension proposed by the terminal.
Title Path: UICC interface during PSM > UICC interface in PSM for E-UTRAN SUSPEND UICC > Acceptance criteria
Content: After step a) the ME reads EF to verify that the SUSPEND UICC command is supported. After step e) the ME deactivates the UICC as specified in 3GPP TS 31.101 . 3) After step g) the ME leaves the PSM and resumes the UICC.

Title Path: UICC interface during eDRX > UICC interface during eDRX for E-UTRAN SUSPEND UICC > Definition and applicability
Content: In order to reduce power consumption when the UE uses extended idle mode DRX cycle, as defined in 3GPP TS 24.301 , in case the UICC supports the UICC suspension mechanism (SUSPEND UICC command), the ME may suspend the UICC during the extended idle mode DRX cycle. In this case, the ME shall resume the UICC successfully before the end of the extended idle mode DRX cycle or before any other transmission to the network.
Title Path: UICC interface during eDRX > UICC interface during eDRX for E-UTRAN SUSPEND UICC > Conformance requirement
Content: In case the UICC supports the UICC suspension mechanism (SUSPEND UICC command), the ME may suspend the UICC during the extended idle mode DRX cycle. In this case, the ME shall resume the UICC successfully before the end of the extended idle mode DRX cycle or before any other transmission to the network. Reference: 3GPP TS 31.102 , clause 5.1.11; TS 24.301 , clauses 5.3.12. TS 23.401 , clause 5.13a. 3GPP TS 31.101 in clauses 6A.1 and 11.1.22.
Title Path: UICC interface during eDRX > UICC interface during eDRX for E-UTRAN SUSPEND UICC > Test purpose

Title Path: Authentication procedure and NAS security context handling for 5G > Authentication procedure for EAP-AKA' > Authentication procedure for EAP-AKA' - Authentication is successful > Definition and applicability
Content: The purpose of the primary authentication and key agreement procedure is to enable mutual authentication between the UE and the network and to provide keying material that can be used between the UE and network in subsequent security procedures. The UE and the AMF shall support the EAP based primary authentication and key agreement procedure. In order to initiate the EAP based primary authentication and key agreement procedure using EAP-AKA', the AUSF shall send an EAP message IE with EAP-request/AKA'-challenge message in the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message. The 5G NAS security context parameters from a full native 5G NAS security context shall be stored on the USIM if the corresponding file is present on the USIM as specified in 3GPP TS 31.102 . If the corresponding file is not present on the USIM, this 5GMM parameters is stored in a non-volatile memory in the ME together with the SUPI from the USIM. The EF contains the 5GS 3GPP access NAS security context as defined in 3GPP TS 24.501 , consisting of K with the associated key set identifier, the UE security capabilities, and the uplink and downlink NAS COUNT values. This file shall contain one record. The EF contains K and K that are generated on the ME using CK and IK as part of AKA procedures as described in 3GPP TS 33.501 .

The UE and the AMF shall support the EAP based primary authentication and key agreement procedure. In order to initiate the EAP based primary authentication and key agreement procedure using EAP-AKA', the AUSF shall send an EAP message IE with EAP-request/AKA'-challenge message in the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message. The 5G NAS security context parameters from a full native 5G NAS security context shall be stored on the USIM if the corresponding file is present on the USIM as specified in 3GPP TS 31.102 . If the corresponding file is not present on the USIM, this 5GMM parameters is stored in a non-volatile memory in the ME together with the SUPI from the USIM. The EF contains the 5GS 3GPP access NAS security context as defined in 3GPP TS 24.501 , consisting of K with the associated key set identifier, the UE security capabilities, and the uplink and downlink NAS COUNT values. This file shall contain one record. The EF contains K and K that are generated on the ME using CK and IK as part of AKA procedures as described in 3GPP TS 33.501 . If service n$^ $133 is "available" in EF , the EF also contains SOR counter and UE parameter update counter associated with the key K as described in 3GPP TS 33.501 and 3GPP TS 31.102 . 15.1A.1.2 Conformance requirement 1) The UE shall support the EAP based primary authentication and key agreement procedure. The ME shall forward the RAND and AUTN received in EAP message IE with EAP-request/AKA'-challenge within the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message to the USIM. The ME shall return the EAP message IE with EAP-response/AKA'-challenge in AUTHENTICATION RESPONSE message. Title Path: Authentication procedure and NAS security context handling for 5G > Authentication procedure for EAP-AKA' > Authentication procedure for EAP-AKA' AUTN fails on the USIM > Definition and applicability
Content: The purpose of the primary authentication and key agreement procedure is to enable mutual authentication between the UE and the network and to provide keying material that can be used between the UE and network in subsequent security procedures. The UE and the AMF shall support the EAP based primary authentication and key agreement procedure. At receipt of the RAND and AUTN, the USIM shall verify the freshness of the AV' by checking whether AUTN can be accepted as described in 3GPP TS 33.102 . If so, the USIM computes a response RES. The USIM shall return RES, CK, IK to the ME. The ME shall derive CK' and IK'. If the verification of the AUTN fails on the USIM, then the USIM and ME shall proceed as described in clause 6.1.3.3 in 3GPP TS 33.501 .
Title Path: Authentication procedure and NAS security context handling for 5G > Authentication procedure for EAP-AKA' > Authentication procedure for EAP-AKA' AUTN fails on the USIM > Conformance requirement
Content: The ME shall forward the RAND and AUTN received in the EAP message IE with EAP-request/AKA'-challenge in the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message to the USIM. If the verification of the AUTN fails on the USIM, then the USIM and ME shall proceed as described in clause 6.1.3.3 in 3GPP TS 33.501 . The ME shall return the EAP-Response/AKA-Synchronization-Failure, when the sequence number in the AUTN parameter is incorrect as described in clause 9.6 of RFC 4187 . Reference: 3GPP TS 33.501 , clause 6.1.3.1 and 6.1.3.3; 3GPP TS 24.501 , clauses 5.4.1.2.2.1. RFC 4187 , clause 9.6.

As a result of successful authentication procedure if service n$^ $122 is "available", the 5G NAS security context parameters shall be stored on the USIM. If service n$^ $123 is "available", the ME shall store the K and K in EF on the USIM. Title Path: Authentication procedure and NAS security context handling for 5G > Authentication procedure for 5G AKA > Authentication procedure 5G AKA AUTN fails on the USIM > Definition and applicability
Content: The purpose of the primary authentication and key agreement procedure is to enable mutual authentication between the UE and the network and to provide keying material that can be used between the UE and network in subsequent security procedures. The UE and the AMF shall support the EAP based primary authentication and key agreement procedure. At receipt of the RAND and AUTN, the USIM shall verify the freshness of the AV' by checking whether AUTN can be accepted as described in TS 33.102 . If so, the USIM computes a response RES. The USIM shall return RES, CK, IK to the ME. If the verification of the AUTN fails on the USIM, then the USIM and ME shall proceed as described in clause 6.1.3. 3 in 3GPP TS 33.501 .
Title Path: Authentication procedure and NAS security context handling for 5G > Authentication procedure for 5G AKA > Authentication procedure 5G AKA AUTN fails on the USIM > Conformance requirement
Content: The ME shall forward the RAND and AUTN received in 5G authentication challenge data within AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message. If the verification of the AUTN fails on the USIM, then the USIM and ME shall proceed as described in clause 6.1.3. 3 in 3GPP TS 33.501 . The ME shall return Synchronization-Failure of AUTH in the AUTHENTICATION FAILURE message. Reference: 3GPP TS 33.501 , clause 6.1.3.2 and 6.1.3.3; 3GPP TS 24.501 , clause 5.4.1.3.7
Title Path: Authentication procedure and NAS security context handling for 5G > Authentication procedure for 5G AKA > Authentication procedure 5G AKA AUTN fails on the USIM > Test purpose
Content: To verify that the ME forwards the RAND and AUTN received in the 5G authentication challenge message to the USIM. To verify that the ME returns the Synchronization-Failure in the AUTHENTICATION FAILURE message if the verification of AUTN failed on the USIM due to a synchronisation failure.

Content: [ a) ] Bring up Cell A and the UE is switched on. Upon reception of an RRCSetupRequest message from the UE, NG-SS transmits an RRCSetup message to the UE followed by reception of an RRCSetupComplete message from the UE. After reception of a REGISTRATION REQUEST message from the UE during registration, the NG-SS initiates the 5G AK' authentication procedure and sends 5G AKA challenge data in the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message contains: ngKSI: [NAS key set identifier:]'000' [TSC:]'0' [Authentication parameter RAND (5G Authentication challenge):]128 bits value [Authentication parameter AUTN (5G Authentication challenge):]128 bits value Using the data received in AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message the ME passes the RAND and AUTN to the USIM. Title Path: Authentication procedure and NAS security context handling for 5G > Authentication procedure for 5G AKA > Authentication procedure for 5G AKA - after SUPI is changed > Definition and applicability
Content: The purpose of the 5G AKA based primary authentication and key agreement procedure is to provide mutual authentication between the UE and the network and to agree on the keys K , K and K . The UE and the AMF shall support the 5G AKA based primary authentication and key agreement procedure. These 5GMM parameters can only be used if the SUPI from the USIM matches the SUPI stored in the non-volatile memory; else the UE shall delete the 5GMM parameters.
Title Path: Authentication procedure and NAS security context handling for 5G > Authentication procedure for 5G AKA > Authentication procedure for 5G AKA - after SUPI is changed > Conformance requirement
Content: The UE shall support the 5G AKA based primary authentication and key agreement procedure. The 5G NAS security context parameters shall be stored on the USIM if the corresponding file is present on the USIM, else the 5GMM parameters shall be stored in the non-volatile memory in the ME together with the SUPI from the USIM. The UE shall delete the 5GMM parameters if the SUPI from the USIM does not match the SUPI stored in the non-volatile memory. Reference: 3GPP TS 33.501 , clause 6.1.3.2; 3GPP TS 24.501 , clauses 5.4.1.3, Annex C.

Title Path: Authentication procedure and NAS security context handling for 5G > Authentication procedure for 5G AKA > 15.2.5 Authentication procedure for multiple registrations 3GPP access 5G AKA - Authentication is successful in different PLMNs
Content: 15.2.5.1 Definition and applicability The UE can be multiple registered in different PLMN's serving networks or in the same PLMN's serving networks. The UE will establish two NAS connections with the network in both cases and the UE uses the same subscription credential(s) for multiple registrations in the same or different serving networks. The UE shall independently maintain and use two different 5G NAS security contexts, one per PLMN's serving network. Each security context shall be established separately via a successful primary authentication procedure with the Home PLMN. The ME shall store the two different 5G NAS security contexts on the USIM if the USIM supports for multiple records of NAS security context storage for multiple registration as specified in 3GPP TS 31.102 . The purpose of the 5G AKA based primary authentication and key agreement procedure is to provide mutual authentication between the UE and the network and to agree on the keys K , K and K . The UE and the AMF shall support the 5G AKA based primary authentication and key agreement procedure. The EF contains the 5GS 3GPP access NAS security context as defined in 3GPP TS 24.501 , consisting of K with the associated key set identifier, the UE security capabilities, and the uplink and downlink NAS COUNT values. This file shall contain two records if service n$^ $136 is "available". The EF contains K and K that are generated on the ME using CK and IK as part of AKA procedures as described in 3GPP TS 33.501 . If service n$^ $133 is "available" in EF , the EF also contains SOR counter and UE parameter update counter associated with the key K as described in 3GPP TS 33.501 and 3GPP TS 31.102 .
Title Path: Authentication procedure and NAS security context handling for 5G > Authentication procedure for 5G AKA > 15.2.5 Authentication procedure for multiple registrations 3GPP access 5G AKA - Authentication is successful in different PLMNs > Conformance requirement
Content: The UE shall support the 5G AKA based primary authentication and key agreement procedure. The USIM shall support multiple records of NAS security context storage for multiple registration (i.e. service n$^ $136 is "available"). The ME shall forward the RAND and AUTN received in AUTHENTICATION REQUEST message to the USIM. The ME shall compute RES* from RES according to Annex A.4 3GPP TS 33.501 and return it in AUTHENTICATION RESPONSE message. As a result of first successful authentication procedure in a PLMN (PLMN 1 over 3GPP access) if service n$^ $122 is "available", the 5G 3GPP access NAS security context parameters shall be stored on the USIM in the first record of the EF . As a result of second successful authentication procedure in another PLMN (PLMN 2 over 3GPP access) if service n$^ $122 and service n$^ $136 is "available", the 5G 3GPP access NAS security context parameters of the PLMN 2 shall be stored on the USIM in the first record of the EF . The second record of the EF contains the 5G 3GPP access NAS security context parameters of the PLMN 1. Reference: 3GPP TS 31.102 , clauses 4.4.11.2, 4.4.11.3, 4.4.11.4, 4.4.11.5 and 4.4.11.6; 3GPP TS 33.501 , clause 6.1.3.2 and 6.3.2; 3GPP TS 24.501 , clause 4.4.2.1, 4.4.2.5, 5.4.1.3 and Annex C.

Title Path: UE Route Selection Policy (URSP) procedure > Pre-configured URSP rules > Support for URSP by USIM > Definition and applicability
Content: As specified in 3GPP TS 24.526 , if the UE has no signalled URSP, and the UE has pre-configured URSPs configured in both the USIM and the ME, then the UE shall use the pre-configured URSP in the USIM. As specified in 3GPP TS 31.102 , the EF in the USIM contains UE Route Selection Policies per PLMN and shall be taken into account by the ME if EF service $^ $ 132 "Support for URSP by USIM" is available.

Title Path: UE Route Selection Policy (URSP) procedure > Pre-configured URSP rules > Support of Signalled URSP > Definition and applicability
Content: The HPLMN pre-configured URSP in the ME and the HPLMN signalled URSP shall be stored in a non-volatile memory in the ME together with the SUPI from the USIM. If the UE has both pre-configured URSP(s) and signalled URSP, the UE shall only use the signalled URSP. For a UE not operating in SNPN access mode, if the UE has no signalled URSP, and the UE has pre-configured URSPs configured in both the USIM and the ME, then the UE shall use the pre-configured URSP in the USIM. The HPLMN pre-configured URSP in the ME shall be stored until a new URSP is configured by HPLMN or the USIM is removed.
Title Path: UE Route Selection Policy (URSP) procedure > Pre-configured URSP rules > Support of Signalled URSP > Conformance requirement
Content: The UE shall support the URSP procedure. If the UE has both pre-configured URSP(s) and signalled URSP, the UE shall only use the signalled URSP. Reference: 3GPP TS 24.526 , clause 4.2.2.2 and 5.2; 3GPP TS 23.503 , clause 6.6.2.

Title Path: CAG list handling > CAG list handling for 5G > Automatic CAG selection with preconfigured CAG list on USIM > Definition and applicability
Content: If MS supports CAG and is pre-configured with a non-empty "CAG information list" stored in the USIM, the MS in automatic PLMN selection mode shall consider a PLMN indicated by an NG-RAN cell only if [ A) ] the cell is a CAG cell and broadcasts a CAG-ID for the PLMN such that there exists an entry with the PLMN ID of the PLMN in the "CAG information list" and the CAG-ID is included in the "Allowed CAG list" of the entry; or the cell is not a CAG cell and: there is no entry with the PLMN ID of the PLMN in the "CAG information list"; or there exists an entry with the PLMN ID of the PLMN in the "CAG information list" but the "indication that the MS is only allowed to access 5GS via CAG cells" is not included in the entry.
Title Path: CAG list handling > CAG list handling for 5G > Automatic CAG selection with preconfigured CAG list on USIM > Conformance requirement
Content: 1) If service n$^ $137 is "available" in EF and preconfigured "CAG information list" is available on USIM, then an ME that supports CAG shall read EF and consider the PLMN indicated by the NG-RAN to perform automatic PLMN selection procedure. 2) If the available CAG cell broadcasts a CAG-ID for the PLMN such that there exists an entry with the PLMN ID of the PLMN in the "CAG information list" and the CAG-ID is included in the "Allowed CAG list" of the entry, then UE shall select the CAG cell. Reference: TS 31.102 , clauses 4.4.11.14. TS 23.122 , clauses 3.8, 4.4.3.1.1 TS 24.501 , clauses 9.11.3.18A
Title Path: CAG list handling > CAG list handling for 5G > Automatic CAG selection with preconfigured CAG list on USIM > Test purpose
Content: To verify that ME only selects the CAG cell if the PLMN ID and CAG ID of the cell is found in the EF (Pre-configured CAG information list) available on USIM.
Title Path: CAG list handling > CAG list handling for 5G > Automatic CAG selection with preconfigured CAG list on USIM > Method of tests > Initial conditions
Content: The NG-SS is configured with the following network parameters, and both cells are switched off: CAG Cell A TAI (MCC/MNC/TAC): 244/083/000001. cag-Identity: 00 00 00 02 CAG Cell B TAI (MCC/MNC/TAC): 244/083/000002. cag-Identity: 00 00 00 09 The default CAG 5G-NR UICC is used and the UICC is installed into the Terminal.
Title Path: CAG list handling > CAG list handling for 5G > Automatic CAG selection with preconfigured CAG list on USIM > Method of tests > Procedure
Content: [ a) ] Bring up CAG cell B, and the UE is switched on. After 5 mins, bring up CAG cell A. c) The UE sends REGISTRATION REQUEST to the available CAG cell A, indicates the registration type IE as "initial registration". The NG-SS sends REGISTRATION ACCEPT with a 5G-GUTI. The UE sends REGISTRATION COMPLETE to NG-SS. UE is switched off, and then Cell A is powered down. CAG Cell B is powered up again with SIB1 modified to indicate new cag-identity 00 00 00 07. The UE is now switched on. The UE sends REGISTRATION REQUEST to CAG Cell B, indicates the registration type IE as "initial registration". UE is switched off, and then NG-SS is powered down.
Title Path: CAG list handling > CAG list handling for 5G > Automatic CAG selection with preconfigured CAG list on USIM > Method of tests > Acceptance criteria
Content: 1) After step a) ME shall not attempt registration to CAG Cell B. 2) At step c) ME shall send REGISTRATION REQUEST to CAG cell A. 3) After step i) ME shall send REGISTRATION REQUEST to CAG cell B.
